Route: /JournalEntry | Automatic and manual entries, manual journals and opening balances
Gathers the entries created automatically by every module (inventory postings, labour and overhead absorption, cost allocation and so on) and also supports manual and adjusting entries. Only the Adjustment type can be posted in a Closing period.
Journal screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.
2
Can be filtered by period, account and source document number.

Manual journal entry
1
Click "Manual journal" at the top right and enter the entry date and a description. The date decides which accounting period the entry falls in.
2
For each line pick an account and enter a debit or a credit — never both on the same line . The drop-down lists only the accounts flagged as manually selectable in the chart of accounts: inventory, the GR/IR accrual and the like, whose balances are maintained by automatic postings, are not offered.
3
The footer shows the running debit and credit totals and the difference. Click "Save"; if the entry does not balance, or the period is closed, the form comes back with the reason.
A Closing period does not accept manual journals: that status only allows adjusting entries, and those are produced by the month-end tasks themselves — revaluation, NRV impairment, the actual-rate re-estimate — not raised by hand from this screen. To add one while closing, cancel the close first.
Correcting a manual journal: reversal
A saved journal is part of the books and can be neither edited nor deleted ; to correct a mistake, reverse it:
1
Open the journal's details from the list, click "Reverse" and pick the reversal date (today by default; it must fall in a period open for posting).
2
The system creates a new journal with debits and credits swapped, whose source number points back to the original; the original stays and its details show "Reversed by X". Then enter a correct manual journal.
Only manual journals can be reversed; each can be reversed once and a reversal cannot itself be reversed. Requires create permission on this screen. To correct an automatic entry, void or redo the source document.
Opening balances (going live mid-year)
Opening balances are simply a manual journal with many lines: the assets on the debit side, the liabilities and equity on the credit side. Adding dozens of lines one at a time is not practical, so the form provides "Paste lines" : copy the four columns — account code, debit, credit, line description — straight from Excel and paste them in.
1
Date the entry the day before go-live so the opening balances sit before live operations begin.
2
After pasting, the screen reports how many lines were filled and how many were skipped. A line is skipped when the code is not in the chart of accounts, or is not flagged as manually selectable — create it or tick the flag under " Finance > Chart of Accounts " first, then paste again.
3
Check that the debit and credit totals in the footer match, then save.
Why some accounts cannot be selected manually: receivables, payables, inventory and similar accounts are posted automatically by shipments, receipts, issues and other documents, each with its own subledger; a manual entry would leave the general ledger out of agreement with the subledger. They are deliberately closed (the form also says so above the lines); make adjustments through the corresponding document, or have accounting enable the account under Chart of Accounts if it is really needed.
Printing
The button on each row of the list (print permission required) opens a printout with a QR code in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. The voucher printout lists, line by line, the account code and name (English account names on the English interface), description, currency and original amount, and debit and credit, with debit and credit totals.

Route: /MonthEnd | The month-end checklist workflow
Guides the month-end close with a checklist: unposted documents in each module, cost re-estimation, booking the assessments and finally closing the period — each item ticked off and recorded, so that nothing is missed before closing.
Month-end close screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.

Run the month-end close
1
Enter the period and click "Search"; the first time, click "Initialize Checklist" to create the 10 steps.
2
Work through the steps in order: for a step with "Run Batch", run it first and then click "Complete"; click "Skip" for a step that does not apply. A later step cannot be completed until every earlier one is completed or skipped.
3
Step 4 "Run Batch" pre-fills this period's figures already saved in Department Actual Cost (one line per work center: "work center:actual labour:actual overhead"); confirming re-costs work orders at the actual rates and posts the adjusting entry. A work center that has labour or setup hours this period but no department cost is rejected and listed — enter 0 if it genuinely had no cost.
4
Step 6 "Run Batch" takes the period-end rates (one line per currency: "currency:rate") and revalues foreign currency balances; "Run ECL" on the same step calculates expected credit losses as at the period end. Step 7 "Run Batch" runs the NRV assessment. These steps only calculate results; nothing is posted yet.
5
Once step 8 is completed the period is in closing and accepts only adjusting entries; to go back and fix data before closing, click "Cancel Closing" on step 8.
6
Clicking "Complete" on step 9 posts the foreign currency revaluation, NRV and ECL results to the ledger (see "Period-end adjusting entries" below), and the outcome is written to that step's notes. Clicking "Complete" on step 10 closes the period.
After step 9 is completed, its notes list the journal numbers posted or why an item was skipped
Period-end adjusting entries (step 9)
Item | Entry | Guide
Foreign currency revaluation | Gain: Dr 1170 AR / 2100 AP, Cr 4190 FX gain
Loss: Dr 5199 FX loss, Cr 1170 / 2100 | One line per invoice. A reversing entry dated the day after the period end is posted automatically — exchange differences on receipts and payments are measured from the invoice's booking rate, so without the reversal they would be recognised twice
NRV inventory write-down | Dr 5240 Inventory write-down loss, Cr 1419 Allowance for inventory valuation loss | Adjusts the allowance to equal this period's assessment; if the assessment falls, the difference is reversed
ECL allowance | Dr 6250 Expected credit impairment loss, Cr 1179 Loss allowance – AR | As for NRV: the allowance is adjusted to equal this period's assessment
It can be run again and only posts the difference, never a duplicate. An assessment that was not run this period is skipped (it is not treated as zero, which would reverse the whole allowance provided in earlier periods). If NRV or ECL is recalculated on its own screen after step 9, step 10 posts the difference once more before closing; if step 9 was skipped, nothing is posted. Foreign currency revaluation and ECL are always assessed as at the period end : only invoices dated on or before the end date count, and payments, receipts and notes confirmed after the end date are added back to the open balance — so when a closed period is reopened and its month-end redone, transactions from the following period do not affect it.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Period | The accounting period (YYYYMM) to close; where no checklist exists yet, the 10 steps are created automatically
Checklist fields
Field | Guide
Step | A fixed order from 1 to 10; no step can be skipped
Step Description | What the step involves at month end (see the table below)
Status | Not done / done; some steps are ticked automatically by the system
Completed At | Timestamp when the step was marked done
Completed By | The user who marked it done
Notes | Notes or exceptions for the step
The ten month-end steps
Step | Guide
1　Confirm all receipts and shipments are posted | so that no document is left unposted and the cost stays complete
2　Count variance adjustments completed | Count sheet differences have to be turned into stock adjustments and posted first
3　Take the WIP valuation snapshot | Freezes the WIP value for period-end valuation and comparison
4　Calculate work order actual cost | "Run Batch" re-costs work order labour and overhead from department actual costs and posts the adjusting entry; "Complete" locks the work order costs as Final
5　Update the AVCO average cost | Recalculate the moving average cost
6　Period-end revaluation of AR and AP (IAS 21) | Foreign currency receivables and payables are revalued at the period-end rate to work out the exchange gain or loss (net of credit notes; overpayments created by a credit note after settlement are revalued too); ECL can also be run on this step. The results are posted at step 9
7　IAS 2 NRV inventory impairment assessment | Compare book cost with net realisable value to work out the impairment (see the NRV assessment screen); the result is posted at step 9
8　Freeze stock movements (period status = Closing) | The period is switched to Closing, after which only adjusting entries are allowed
9　Create the period-end adjusting entries | Clicking "Complete" posts the foreign currency revaluation, NRV and ECL results to the ledger (see period-end adjusting entries )
10　Close the period (period status = Closed) | Runs the pre-closing audit first; once it passes the period is switched to Closed and accepts no further postings. If step 9 was completed, any assessment difference is posted first

Route: /NrvAssessment | Inventory net realisable value impairment assessment
Compares inventory cost with net realisable value under IAS 2, and works out the loss on items whose cost exceeds NRV. The entry is posted at step 9 of Month-End Closing (Dr 5240 Inventory write-down loss / Cr 1419 Allowance for inventory valuation loss); the allowance is adjusted to equal this period's assessment, and if the assessment falls the difference is reversed.
NRV net realisable value assessment screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.
2
Enter the assessment period and the selling price basis, run the assessment and review the suggested provision line by line.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Period (YYYYMM) | The accounting period to assess or query
Field | Guide
Period | Accounting period this assessment belongs to
Item | Item being assessed; items with no sales in the 90 days up to the period end are left out because no selling price can be estimated. Stock in customer-supplied warehouses belongs to the customer and is not assessed
Qty on Hand | Quantity on hand at the period end (movements after the end date are backed out, so redoing a reopened period is not affected by later activity)
Carrying Cost | Unit carrying cost at the period end: the moving average for average-cost items, and the remaining cost-layer value ÷ quantity for FIFO items
NRV Price | Expected selling price: the weighted average over sales invoice lines in the 90 days up to the period end, in local currency per stock unit (Σ local amount ÷ Σ stock quantity)
Selling Cost | Estimated selling cost = NRV unit price × selling cost rate (set as a system parameter)
NRV | Net realisable value = NRV unit price − selling cost
Impairment Loss | max(0, (book cost − NRV) × quantity on hand). It is 0 when the book cost does not exceed NRV, and nothing is provided for

Route: /TrialBalance | Account-level reconciliation before closing
Lists the opening balance, period debits and credits, and closing balance of every account, and states at the top whether total debits equal total credits . It sits between "Management Journal" and "Month-end close" because that is what it is for: the last check before closing .
Trial balance screenshot: the green banner at the top shows that total debits equal total credits
There is already a balance audit — why this report?
The data audit checks per-voucher balance — each voucher debits equal credits. But "every voucher balances" is not "the account balances are right" : a missed posting, a duplicated posting, or a mistyped account code are all invisible at that level, because each voucher on its own is valid. The trial balance looks at the account level , and it is the only place to reconcile the whole set before exporting the entries to an external accounting system.

1
Open "Accounting > Trial Balance".
2
Pick a closing period (required). Leaving from period blank means "since inception": the opening balance is then 0 and the period columns cover everything.
3
Accounts whose opening and period figures are all zero are hidden by default — otherwise the page is mostly zeros. Tick "Show zero-balance accounts" for the full list.

C.H: Trial Balance › How to read it
C.T:
The top line is the point
Green means total debits equal total credits and the period balances as a whole. Red means the ledger is out of balance — do not close the period , and the amount it is out of balance by is shown. The normal entry paths cannot produce a one-sided entry, but data repairs, imports or a posting interrupted halfway can leave one behind, and this report is how you see it.
Profit and loss accounts have a non-zero opening balance — that is not an error
This system deliberately does not perform period-end closing : accounts 4xxx–8xxx are not reset into retained earnings at the year boundary. The books of record live in an external accounting system, and closing is the general ledger's job — doing it here as well would produce two competing sets of closing entries. So across years, the opening balance of a profit and loss account is the cumulative total since inception . The "Net Profit (Unclosed)" card on the balance sheet reports the same thing.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
From period | Blank means since inception. This field decides which entries count as "opening" and which as "this period"
To period | Required. Closing balances are accumulated up to and including this period
Show zero-balance accounts | Also lists accounts with no opening balance and no movement; only needed when checking the full chart of accounts
Report fields
Field | Guide
Account / Name | Taken from the entries. Accounts missing from the master are still listed (a historical entry may reference a deleted account) rather than silently dropped
Opening | Cumulative total before the start period, signed by account nature: assets are positive on the debit side, liabilities and revenue positive on the credit side
Debit / Credit | Raw movement amounts within the range, without the sign convention. The totals of these two columns must be equal
Closing | Opening ± movement. Every row satisfies "opening + debit − credit = closing" (reversed for credit-normal accounts)

Menu: Approval Management → Approval Template Settings | Permission: per permission settings
An approval template defines one approval route : who signs, and in what order. A template does nothing on its own; it has to be attached to a document type under Document Approval Settings before documents of that type follow the route.
Approval template settings screenshot (illustrative; the templates shown depend on your data)

Field | Required | Guide
Template name | Required | The name you recognise it by, such as "Purchase order, three levels". It is what you pick from the drop-down in the document approval settings.
Document type it is for |  | Records which kind of document the route was designed for, to help administrators tell templates apart.
Skip repeated approver |  | With this on, when the approver resolved for a step is somebody who has already signed , that step is passed automatically instead of asking them to sign twice. Skipped steps are still recorded in the history.

Once a template exists, open it to manage its steps. Steps run in order and the system keeps the numbering: a new step is added at the end, the arrows move a step up or down, and deleting one renumbers the rest automatically.
The step panel that opens from a template: the existing steps in order, with move up, move down, edit and delete on the right, and the form for a new step below
The three kinds of approver
Type | How the system finds the approver
Direct Supervisor | From the requester's role at the moment of submission , the system finds that role's organization unit and takes a user under its parent unit. Nobody is named, so the route follows changes in the organization.
Role Approver | You name a role; whoever holds it sees the request while they are in that role . This suits rules stated by job rather than by person, such as "signed by the purchasing manager".
Specific User | You name one person. It is the most explicit, but the template has to be changed by hand when that person leaves or moves on.
Before using the "Direct Supervisor" type, make sure the organization is complete: if the requester's role has no organization unit, if that unit has no parent, or if no user sits under the parent, the step resolves to nobody . The document is still submitted, yet lands in nobody's pending list and no error is shown. See My Pending / All Approval Requests under "Unassigned approver".

Creating an approval route
1
Choose "Approval Management > Approval Template Settings" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to load the existing templates.
2
Click "Add", enter the name and the document type it is for, turn on skip-repeated-approver if you want it, and save.
3
Open the template and add the steps one by one: choose the kind of approver and name the role or the person (the supervisor type needs neither).
4
Use the arrows to set the order; the first step is whoever signs first after submission.
5
Finally attach the template to a real document type under "Document Approval Settings"; only then does the route start working.

C.H: Approval Template Settings › Steps are locked while approvals are in flight
C.T:
While this template has requests that are still unsigned , adding, changing, deleting and moving steps are all blocked , with a message asking you to wait until the approvals finish or are withdrawn. This is deliberate: changing the route would leave running requests without a next stop, stranded and impossible to complete.
1
Filter "All Approval Requests" by status to see which requests are holding things up.
2
Have the approvers sign them, or have the requesters withdraw them.
3
Come back and adjust the steps once none are left.
A step already referenced by past approval records cannot be deleted even when nothing is in flight, because deleting it would leave the historical trail without its basis. In that situation create a new template rather than dismantling the old one.

C.H: Approval Template Settings › Deleting a template
C.T:
Reason it is blocked | What to do
A document approval setting uses it | Point that setting at another template first, or turn "Requires approval" off.
Approvals are still running | Wait until they are signed or withdrawn.
Once the checks pass, the template is deleted together with all of its steps.
The results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the template name, the document type it is for and the number of steps.

Menu: Approval Management → My Pending / All Approval Requests | Permissions: read / update
Approval has two entry points, and this page covers both: My Pending Approvals is each approver's own to-do list, and All Approval Requests lets managers see every request, track down ones that are stuck and reassign the approver.
My pending approvals screenshot (illustrative; the data depends on your own to-do list)

C.H: My Pending / All Approval Requests › My Pending Approvals
C.T:
The list shows only what is assigned to you . That is decided by your account and by the role currently in effect : when a step targets a role, the request only appears while you have switched to that role.
A colleague says they submitted it, but my list is empty: the most common reason is that you are in the wrong role . Switch to the role that has the approval right under personal settings at the top right and look again. If it is still empty, the request may have no approver resolved at all (see "Unassigned approver" below).
Signing a request
1
Choose "Approval Management > My Pending Approvals" in the left-hand menu.
2
Click the document number to view the original document and see what you are signing.
3
Click to process it, choose what to do in the panel and add a comment; the comment stays in the approval history.
4
Submit. If further steps remain the request moves to the next approver; if this was the last step the document is approved.
The three ways to process a request
Action | Result
Approve | Moves to the next step; on the last step the document becomes approved and takes effect.
Reject | The flow ends there and then , and the document does not take effect. The requester has to deal with it separately.
Return for revision | The document goes back to the requester, who may change it and submit it again . Unlike a rejection, the flow is not closed.
You can also sign on a phone
The mobile app has the same pending list, so signing on either side removes it from the other. The phone shows the amount, plant, header fields and the first few lines — enough to decide; open the desktop app when you need the whole document.
Two differences to know: the phone offers only Approve and Reject — there is no "Return for revision" , so use the desktop for that; and only document types whose content can actually be shown can be signed there (14 today), while the rest are visible but say to use the desktop. See My Approvals on mobile .

C.H: My Pending / All Approval Requests › Approval history
C.T:
Every request has a history: each step in order, with the approver, the action, the time and the comment. When a step was signed by a delegate , the history also records on whose behalf they signed. Steps that were skipped automatically are recorded too.
The content and history of a request are visible only to those involved — the requester, the current approver and anyone who has already signed — plus people who may read "All Approval Requests". Somebody else's request number will not open for you.

C.H: My Pending / All Approval Requests › Withdrawing a request
C.T: Submitted by mistake? Only the requester can withdraw a request, and only while it is still running. The record returns to draft, and can be changed and submitted again.

C.H: My Pending / All Approval Requests › Delegates (while you are away)
C.T:
From Delegate settings at the top right of "My Pending Approvals" you can name your delegate and the period they cover (a start and end date). When the setting is in effect:
1
Requests assigned to you during the period go straight to your delegate's list.
2
Requests already sitting in your list are moved across too , and the message after saving tells you how many were moved.
3
When the delegate signs, the history records that they signed on your behalf.
If the delegate happens to be the requester of that particular document, the system does not hand it to them — nobody signs off their own submission by proxy — and it stays with the original approver.

C.H: My Pending / All Approval Requests › All Approval Requests
C.T:
This screen lists requests in every status , filtered by status and document type and sorted by document type, status or creation time. The document type column shows the name in the interface language (such as "Purchase Order"); the filter box matches the document type code (such as PurchaseOrder , partial input allowed), and sorting also follows the code. Read permission for "All Approval Requests" is required to open it.
All approval requests screenshot (illustrative; the data depends on the search criteria)
Finding stuck requests: unassigned approver
Ticking Unassigned only lists requests that are still running yet have no approver at all. Such a request appears in nobody's pending list , raises no error, and simply sits there. It happens when a supervisor step cannot resolve a person: the requester's role has no organization unit, the unit has no parent, or no user sits under the parent unit.
1
Tick "Unassigned only" on "All Approval Requests" and click "Filter" to find them.
2
Click "Reassign Approver", choose who should take it over, give a reason and submit; the request then appears in their pending list.
3
The lasting fix is to go back to Organization Structure and Role Management , and complete the tree and the roles' organization units — otherwise the next submission gets stuck the same way.
Reassigning requires update permission on "All Approval Requests": somebody with read permission alone sees the list but cannot reassign. Also, only requests that are still running can be reassigned; approved or rejected ones cannot.

Menu: Approval Management → Document Approval Settings | Permission: per permission settings
Document approval settings are the master switch for approval : they decide which kind of document needs approval and, when it does, which approval template it follows. A document type not set up here is effective on save, with no approval .
Document approval settings screenshot (illustrative; the settings shown depend on your data)

Field | Required | Guide
Document type name | Required | The name people read, such as "Purchase Requisition". It can be changed at any time.
Type code | Required | The English code the program matches on, such as PurchaseOrder . It cannot be changed once created , and it has to match exactly the code the system actually uses (see the list below).
Requires approval |  | With it off, documents of this type are not submitted for approval; the template field is cleared automatically when you turn it off.
Approval template |  | When approval is required, this is the route it follows. Requiring approval without choosing a template has the same effect as not requiring it .
A mistyped type code produces no error — it simply never takes effect: the system looks up this setting using the code built into the program. If the spelling or capitalisation differs, no setting is found and the document is treated as needing no approval, taking effect immediately. Always create one real document and check that it is actually submitted .

C.H: Document Approval Settings › Settings are per plant
C.T:
Every setting belongs to the plant you were in when you created it , and no other. This means:
Situation | Result
You set up purchase-order approval in plant A only | Purchase orders in plant A need approval; in plant B they take effect on save.
Several plants need approval | You have to switch to each plant and create it there ; there is no way to set it once for the whole company.
A second entry for the same type in the same plant | Is blocked, with a message that the setting already exists for this plant.

Turning on approval for a document type
1
Create the template and its steps under "Approval Template Settings" first.
2
Check that the plant shown at the top right is the one you mean to configure.
3
Choose "Approval Management > Document Approval Settings" in the left-hand menu, click "Search", then "Add".
4
Enter the name and the type code, turn "Requires approval" on, choose the template and save.
5
Test it with a real document of that type: after saving it should say it has been submitted, and appear in the approver's "My Pending Approvals".
Suspending approval for a document type
Open the setting and turn "Requires approval" off; there is no need to delete it. Documents created afterwards take effect immediately, while requests already running are unaffected and still have to be signed or withdrawn.

C.H: Document Approval Settings › Deleting a setting
C.T: While the document type still has approvals in progress , the deletion is blocked and the message names the type. Let those requests be signed or withdrawn first.
The results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the name, the type code, whether approval is required and which template is attached.

Submitting, approving and returning documents, and the settings that decide which documents need signing and by whom
Approval has three parts, and the order to set them up in is first the template, then the document type it is attached to, and only then are there requests to sign :
1
The approval template defines the steps of a route and who signs each one.
2
The document approval setting decides which kind of document follows which route; a type that is not set up is never submitted and takes effect on save.
3
My Pending Approvals is the list approvers use day to day, while managers oversee everything — and rescue stuck requests — from "All Approval Requests".
Approval settings are per plant: a document approval setting applies only to the plant you were in when you created it. If several plants need approval, switch to each and set it up there.

C.H: Approval Management › My Pending / All Approval Requests
C.T: Approving, rejecting, returning for revision, viewing the history, withdrawing a request, setting a delegate, and reassigning as a manager.
What steps make up an approval route: supervisor, a named role or a named person, plus skipping a repeated approver.

Which kinds of document need approval and which template they follow; the settings are per plant.
Approval routes depend on the organization structure and the roles, which are covered under System Administration (SYS) .

Route: /ContainerUnit | Reusable physical boxes: fixed QR labels, current contents and history
The container master defines container types ; this screen manages the individual physical boxes . Each box has a fixed box number, printed as a QR label and stuck on the box for long-term use. Every time a box is filled it is linked to a new lot (by giving box numbers in receiving by box in production completion ), so scanning the box tells you what is inside, how much is left and which location it is in.
Rule: never mix contents in a box. A box holds one lot of one item only (a box used in production: the output of one operation of one work order only). The system only records which lot a box is linked to and reads the quantity straight from that lot in the stock ledger; if a box is mixed, what the system shows is not what is in the box.

Status | Guide
Empty | Not linked to a lot, or the linked lot is down to zero in the ledger (fully issued, shipped or scrapped). It can be filled again; the system works this out automatically , with no manual return step.
In use | The linked lot still has stock on hand, so the box cannot be filled with anything else.
In process | Production output of one operation of a work order was reported into it (work in process, not yet received). Only the same work order can keep using it; once the work order is closed or voided the box automatically counts as empty.
Off-site | The box's lot has left the plant in full with a shipment, outsource issue, loan, sample shipment, return to supplier or cross-plant transfer, so the box went with the goods. The system works this out automatically ; when the box comes back it must be recovered before it is empty again, and until then it cannot be filled. A box whose lot was used up by material issues or scrap is still in the plant and is empty.
Inactive | A damaged or retired box. It can no longer be filled; its data and history are kept.

Create boxes and print labels
1
Click "Create Boxes", choose the container type, enter a box number prefix (BX is prefilled) and a quantity, then click "Create". Box number = prefix-5-digit sequence (e.g. BX-00001), continuing from the highest number used with that prefix, unique company-wide.
2
Search for the new boxes and click "Print labels on this page" (or the printer icon on a single box), then stick the labels on the boxes. The label's QR code is the box number and does not show the contents : the contents change each time the box is filled, and scanning the box number shows what is in it now.
Fill and move boxes
1
In production completion, tick "Receive by box" and scan the boxes to fill into the "Box numbers" field in order, or click "Fill in empty boxes" to fill in empty boxes of that type. The number of box numbers must equal the number of boxes; on receipt, box 1's lot is linked to the first box number, and so on. See production completion .
2
To relocate a whole box, use a stock transfer : scan the box number into the line's lot field and the box's current lot, item, source location and full quantity are filled in.

C.H: Boxes (Container Units) › Packing at put-away, packing existing stock and re-boxing
C.T:
1
When putting away a receipt (or a loan-in, sales return and so on), scan an empty box into "Fill box" in Warehouse Operations or on the phone put-away screen . Leave the lot blank and the system creates a new one (document-line-sequence); after put-away the box is linked to that lot. You can enter your own lot instead, but it must be one that has not been used.
2
To pack loose goods already on hand, click "Pack" above the list, scan the empty box, enter the product code, choose what to pack (location and lot) and the quantity. The system relabels those goods with a new lot in the same location (quantity and cost unchanged, recorded as a posted stock transfer ) and links the box to the new lot. An empty box's details panel also has "Pack".
3
Re-boxing (the old box is damaged, or a whole box is emptied into another one): in "Pack", scan the old box into "From box" and its product, location, lot and quantity are filled in; afterwards the old box's lot is down to zero and it becomes empty automatically. To undo packing or re-boxing, void that transfer.

C.H: Boxes (Container Units) › Use boxes during production
C.T:
1
When reporting production on a dispatch , scan the box into the "Box No." field (on the phone, the container QR scan also accepts a box number). The good quantity is recorded on that box, and the box is linked to this operation of this work order. One operation can report into the same box several times; the quantities add up.
2
Hand the whole box to the next operation: when the next station reports, it scans the same box number . The box is taken over by that station, and its quantity restarts from that station's reports (the previous station's output has been handed on).
3
After the last operation, scan these boxes when ticking "Receive by box" in production completion ("Fill in empty boxes" lists this work order's in-process boxes first). The boxes then become "In use" and are linked to the new finished-goods lots.
If a desktop report scans a box that already holds some other work order's work in process, or an inventory lot, the whole report is rejected; swap in an empty box. A phone report (which may be resent after a lost connection) is not rejected: the report is saved, the box is not linked, and the screen shows why. An in-process box's quantity is what was put in; if only part of it is taken between operations the system does not track that, so clear the box or swap in an empty one.

C.H: Boxes (Container Units) › Leaving the plant and coming back
C.T:
1
When issuing a whole box, scan the box number in the issue panel of Warehouse Operations (or on the phone pick screen ) and the box's lot and quantity are filled in. Once a shipment, outsource issue or similar document has issued all of that lot, the box automatically shows as "Off-site", and the details panel shows which document it left with and the party it went to.
2
When boxes come back, click "Recover" above the list and scan the box numbers in, one per line (or click "Recover" in a single box's details panel). Recovered boxes become empty and can be filled again. A box that is not off-site cannot be recovered, and the reason is listed.
3
Boxes sent to a second plant with a cross-plant transfer : after the destination plant receives the goods, use "Recover" on the destination plant's Boxes screen for those box numbers. The boxes move to the destination plant, and since their lot has been received there they are "In use" straight away and are used there as normal.
4
The panels and printouts of shipments, loans out, outsource issues, purchase returns, sample shipments and cross-plant transfers list "Boxes shipped" below the lines: which boxes the document's lots belong to, how much each held, and whether each box has come back. You do not enter box numbers on the document itself.

C.H: Boxes (Container Units) › Look up and maintain
C.T:
1
The search box accepts a scan of the QR code on the box, or a lot or item number. Click "Details" to see the current contents (item, lot, quantity per location, filling document) and the latest 50 history entries.
2
"Clear": use it when the box has been emptied physically but its lot still has stock in the ledger (for example the remainder is now held loose). It only removes the link between box and lot and does not change stock .
3
"Deactivate": use it when a box is damaged or retired; it can be reactivated later.
If the details panel says the box's lot is in more than one location, someone relocated only part of the box, which means it was taken out of the box. Check the physical box.

Create boxes
Field | Guide
Container Type | Required Which container type the boxes belong to (container master, active only)
Box number prefix | Required 1 to 10 letters or digits, converted to upper case
Number of boxes | Required 1 to 500 at a time
List columns
Field | Guide
Box No. | The content of the fixed QR label; cannot be changed once created
Status | Empty / In use / In process / Off-site / Inactive; see "Box status" above
Item / Lot No. | Item and lot the box is linked to while in use; blank for empty boxes
Left with | The document an off-site box left the plant with

Qty | In use: total on-hand quantity of that lot across this plant's locations (taken from the stock ledger), not a separately kept figure. In process: total good quantity this operation reported into the box

Route: /BAS/DocNumberConfig | Number formats for each document type
Doc number config defines the automatic numbering format of each document type (purchase request, purchase order, work order, …), including prefix, date format and sequence length. The system generates a unique number from these rules whenever a document is created.
Doc number config screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Required | Guide
Document Type | Required | The document type it belongs to (e.g. PUR = purchase order, REQ = purchase request); system types cannot be changed
Prefix |  | Fixed text at the start of the number (e.g. PO, REQ, WO)
Date Format |  | Date format inserted after the prefix: none, YYYY, YYYYMM, YYYYMMDD
Sequence Length | Required | Number of digits the sequence is padded to (e.g. 4 = 0001–9999)

Active |  | Once inactive, this type no longer issues numbers automatically

While editing a doc number config, the "Preview" box on the right shows a live sample of the number produced by the current settings. For example:
Prefix | Date Format | Sequence Length | Sample number
PO | YYYYMM | 4 | PO2026060001
WO | YYYYMMDD | 3 | WO20260601001
REQ | YYYY | 5 | REQ202600001
CTR | None | 6 | CTR000001

Editing an existing setting
1
Go to "Basic Data > Doc Number Config" and find the document type to adjust (e.g. PUR).
2
Click the document type code to open the edit panel.
3
Adjust the prefix, date format or sequence length; the preview on the right updates immediately.
4
Check that the preview format is correct, then click "Save".
Note: Once the system is live and documents exist, avoid changing the prefix or date format, as it can make numbers non-continuous or duplicated. If a change is unavoidable, adjust the starting sequence value at the same time.
When you choose a monthly sequence reset, also pick a date format containing "YYYYMM" so the same sequence in different months cannot collide (PO2026050001 and PO2026060001 are then clearly different documents).

C.H: Doc Number Config › Why numbers are never reused after the reset cycle changes
C.T:
The sequence is counted per period: a yearly reset counts within the year period (e.g. 2026 ), a monthly reset counts within the month period (such as 202607 ). Changing the reset cycle switches to another period counter that starts from 1, but the date part printed in the number (such as 2607 ) does not change with it, so a number that has already been used could be issued again — and saving it then produces Duplicate document numbers or "A posting record already exists; duplicate posting is not allowed" and similar errors.
continues automatically when numbers are issued : when issuing a number the system compares the period counters of the same document date under every reset cycle and continues from the largest one. So however and whenever the cycle was changed (on this screen, directly in the database, or by restoring a backup), an old number is never issued again — at most there is a gap in the numbering 。
normal year-end and month-end resets are unaffected : only the period counters derived from the same document date are compared, so 2027 never sees a 2026 number and the sequence still restarts at 1 when it should.
When the reset cycle is changed on this screen the system first realigns the sequence, within the same transaction as the save.
so after the cycle is changed the numbering may show gaps (for example 00002–00006 are skipped). The gap is deliberate — it prevents duplicates — and is normal.
Still to be avoided: changing Prefix or Date Format changes how the number looks, and the system cannot tell whether a new number duplicates an old one. Avoid changing it after go-live; if you must, first make sure the new format cannot reproduce an existing number.

Plant parameter overview screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

This report has no query criteria . The parameter list is a fixed 12 rows and the number of plants is a single digit, so everything loads at once. Opening the screen is the whole result.
Criterion | Guide
Plant scope | Not an input. It follows the signed-in user's role: if the role has plant assignments, only those plants are listed; if it has no assignment restriction (for example a management role attached to the root organization unit), every plant is listed

Field | Guide
Parameter | Lists the plant-scopable parameters defined by PlantParamCatalog (currently 11). The grey text under each name is the actual parameter key (identical to the Key column in SystemParams / PlantParams)
N plant(s) overridden | Yellow badge next to the parameter name. N is the number of plants that currently set their own value. Hidden when no plant overrides it
Global Value | The value set on the Core System Parameters screen — the value every non-overriding plant actually uses
Per-plant columns | One column per plant, headed by plant code and name. A yellow badge means the plant overrides the parameter (the override value is shown); grey 「Inherited」 means the plant has no override row and follows the global value

C.H: Plant Parameter Overview › How a value is resolved
C.T:
For any plant, the effective value of a parameter is the first of the following that yields a result:
1
Plant override — the plant has a row in PlantParams, shown as a yellow badge. Note that overriding to an empty value still counts as an override: it shows as (empty), not Inherited.
2
Global value — set on the Core System Parameters screen. Every plant marked Inherited uses this value, so changing the global value affects all of them at once.
3
Built-in default — used when neither layer is set. This layer is not visible in the report; the Global Value column will be blank.
A common use before go-live: separate 「deliberately different per plant」 from 「forgot to set it」. A column that is entirely Inherited means the parameter is currently uniform system-wide; when exactly one plant carries a yellow badge, it is worth confirming that this was intended.

The Export Excel button in the top right writes the whole matrix out with the same column order as the screen (parameter, module, global value, then one column per plant). It requires print permission.

C.H: Product Category › Who actually uses these two defaults
C.T:
The default warehouse and location act as a fallback at processing time : in the situations below, if the document does not name a warehouse or location the system reads these two values from the item's category; when it cannot, the action either stops or falls back elsewhere.
Situation | What happens if it is not set
Goods shipment, sales return | Neither document has a warehouse or location field , so this fallback is always used. If it is not set the document is rejected at confirmation ("no location given and the product category has no default") — this happens even on a single-warehouse deployment
Backflushed material | Backflush has no staging order and no field for a source, so only this value is available; failing that it falls back to the completion receipt's own warehouse. With split warehouses the whole work order then cannot be received — see Production Putaway
Goods receipt, purchase return | Used in simplified mode when the document does not name a warehouse or location
Outsource receipt (not simplified) | Phone receiving does not ask for a warehouse: returned goods go here once they pass inspection. If a product that needs inspection has none, confirming the receipt is blocked with the product named (previously it was accepted, and passed goods then stayed in quarantine)
Auto-deducting send-out material, inspection at receipt | Send-out material is deducted from here; goods that pass inspection at receipt are stocked here. If unset, the receipt is blocked with the product named
Create at least the three basic categories — raw material, WIP and finished goods — each with its own warehouse and location : all three situations above work on the location, so a setting without one counts as not set.

C.H: Warehouse › Warehouse type and available quantity
C.T:
Besides classification, the warehouse type also decides whether its stock counts toward plant-level available quantity (the basis for MRP and material readiness):
Type | Counts toward available quantity | Purpose
Raw | Yes | Source for goods receipt and material issue
WIP | Yes | Semi-finished goods in process
Finished | Yes | Source for production put-away and shipping
Quarantine | No | Holding area before IQC release; stock cannot be used until it is released
Outsource | Yes | Destination warehouse for material sent to outsourcing
Scrap | Yes | Collection warehouse for scrap documents and process losses. The system does not exclude it from available quantity automatically, so leave "MRP Warehouse" unchecked to stop MRP treating scrap as usable stock
Staging | Yes | Holding area filled by staging orders, waiting to be issued to production
Customer Supplied | Yes | The only valid destination for material supplied by a customer (customer-supplied receipt CI and return CR). The material can be issued normally for that customer's orders, so it counts toward availability, but its unit cost is always 0 and it never enters the moving average — it belongs to the customer and is not our asset
Why staging warehouses still count toward available quantity: Material in a staging warehouse is already reserved and locked when the staging order is confirmed, so available quantity has been deducted once. Excluding it again the way quarantine stock is excluded would deduct the same material twice, understating plant-wide availability and making MRP raise purchase requests that are not needed. Quarantine warehouses have no reservation mechanism, so they must be excluded by warehouse type.
Why customer-supplied material must go to a customer-supplied warehouse: The moving-average cost pool is keyed by plant and item, and the denominator is every on-hand unit of that item in the plant. Customer-supplied material received into an ordinary warehouse therefore enters that denominator, depressing the unit cost of your own stock and spreading into the cost of goods sold of every later shipment — the books still balance and nothing reports an error. Separating by item or by lot does not help, because the denominator sums the whole plant anyway; only the warehouse type separates them. Posting blocks customer-supplied movements aimed at any other warehouse type, and the Data Audit report has a dedicated check that finds customer-supplied stock already sitting in the wrong warehouse; the fix is to transfer that stock into a customer-supplied warehouse.

If a purchase debit note is issued after an invoice has been paid in full (for example goods were returned to the supplier), we have overpaid: the invoice's "Outstanding" becomes negative , and it shows up both in the invoice list on this screen and in AP Aging . 1
Supplier refunds us: enter a negative amount (for example −105) against the overpaid invoice only; "Payment Amount" follows to −105. Choose the bank account the refund arrives in, then save and confirm. The bank balance goes up, and the ledger is debited to Bank and credited to Accounts Payable.

Route: /ChartOfAccount | The company-wide chart of accounts
The chart of accounts holds the account definitions shared across the whole company . Accounts are not per plant: every plant posts to the same set. The financial statements use the account type to decide which section an entry lands in and which side counts as positive.
System accounts and your own accounts are two different things: the ones marked "System" — inventory, accounts payable, the GR/IR accrual and so on — are used when the program posts automatically, so their code and account type cannot be changed and they cannot be deleted . Changing them would silently put automatic entries in the wrong report section. Only the name, the remarks, the manual-selectable flag and the active flag can be edited.
Chart of accounts screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Account name | Required | Up to 100 characters. The name is written onto the journal entry as well, so that the ledger reads sensibly.
Account type | Required | Determines the debit/credit direction and which report section the account lands in. The values line up with the leading digit of the code: 1 asset, 2 liability, 3 equity (balance sheet) and 4 revenue, 5 cost of goods sold, 6 operating expense, 7 other income, 8 other expense (profit and loss). Assets and cost/expense accounts are debit-normal ; liabilities, equity and revenue are credit-normal .

C.H: Chart of Accounts › How it relates to manual invoices
C.T:
When a manual AP or AR invoice is entered, every line must have an account , and the choices come from the accounts in this master that are ticked as manually selectable and of a matching type : an AP invoice offers only cost and expense accounts (5, 6, 8), an AR invoice only revenue accounts (4, 7). It is also the only source : a line without an account is refused outright, and the system does not work one out from the product category or anywhere else.
That is exactly why this master exists: costs such as electricity or freight have no product number, and deriving the account from one would mean inventing a dummy product for "electricity", complete with a product category — a dummy that would then show up in every product drop-down, in MRP and in the stock reports.

C.H: Chart of Accounts › Deleting an account
C.T:
A system account can never be deleted. An account already referenced by an invoice or a journal entry likewise cannot be deleted ; the system blocks it and says so. The reason is that once it is gone, the account code on those lines can no longer be resolved to a name, and the journal entries lose their readable account description.
To retire an account, untick "Active" rather than deleting it: once inactive it can no longer be chosen on new invoices, while existing invoices and journal entries display exactly as before. This is the right way to handle an account that is no longer in use.

The FIN (Finance) module manages the payment and receipt cycle: confirming a goods or outsource receipt creates the AP invoice automatically, confirming a shipment creates the AR invoice (which can also be raised by hand), and payments and receipts allocate against the invoices and update the bank account balance immediately. Foreign currency transactions are booked at the transaction-date rate, and realised exchange gains and losses are recognised automatically on settlement (IAS 21). Aging analysis keeps overdue receivables and payables in view.

SmartFactory MES is an enterprise system that brings manufacturing execution, purchasing, inventory, orders, quality, finance and closing together. Every department uses it through the same browser interface, and it supports multiple plants, multiple languages and mobile devices. Documents flow between modules automatically: orders drive MRP for production and purchasing, receipts and shipments create AP and AR invoices, and every stock and accounting movement is subject to the accounting period lock, so the books and the physical stock stay in step.

Master Data | BAS | Shared master data: companies, products, warehouses, work centers, currencies and more

4-2 Module manuals
Master Data Management (BAS)
The master data shared by the whole system: companies and suppliers, products, warehouses, work centers, currencies, tax codes, shifts and document numbering rules. Set these up first, before going live.
Manufacturing (MFG)
Routings and BOMs, the MRP run, production scheduling and dispatch, shop-floor reporting, completion receipt and work order cost, plus production analysis such as utilisation and OEE.
Purchasing (PUR)
Requisition → purchase order → goods receipt (IQC) → return; delivery chasing, the supplier scorecard and purchase price analysis.
Outsource Management (OSP)
Outsource quotation and purchasing, issuing and returning material to the subcontractor, outsource receipt with scrap penalty, outsource rework and progress tracking; a receipt creates the outsource AP invoice automatically.
Order Management (ORD)
Sales and internal orders, shipments and sales returns; orders drive MRP; analysis such as sales ranking, trend and delivery attainment.
Quality Control (QCR)
The three inspection stages IQC/IPQC/FQC (MIL-STD-1916 sampling), closed-loop NCR disposition, instrument calibration and SPC process capability.
Inventory Management (INV)
Inventory documents and warehouse operations (put-away and picking), stock counting, in-plant and cross-plant transfers, outsource and rework material issue and return, and inventory health analysis.
Finance (FIN)
Receipts and shipments create AP and AR invoices automatically, with payment and receipt allocation, bank account balances and AR/AP aging analysis, plus multi-currency exchange gains and losses.
Closing / IFRS (ACT)
The accounting period lock, the journal, the month-end checklist, departmental actual costs and the IFRS assessments (NRV, ECL and revaluation).
Management Reports (RPT)
The management dashboard, income statement and balance sheet, multi-dimensional margin and contribution analysis, and the outsource reconciliation report.
Want to be walked through a flow? Every flow above has a matching guided tutorial , which takes you screen by screen and step by step through it, with optional voice narration. The tutorials are simulated with screenshots and never touch real data.

Q: I submitted a document for approval and now I cannot find it. Where is it?
A: A submitted document is still in the list, with the status "pending approval". Select that status in the query criteria to find it.
Q: A red error message appears after I save. What does it mean?
A: Fix the required fields or format errors named in the message and save again.
Q: Shipping says "not enough stock". Why?
A: Check the real balance under "Stock Balance Enquiry" and see whether a staging order or another reservation is holding the stock.
Q: Posting says "the period is closed". What now?
A: The accounting period the transaction date falls in has been closed by finance. Check the date, or ask finance to help.
Q: How do I change the language?
A: Click the language icon at the top right and choose 繁體中文 or English.

Route: /CrossPlantTransfer | Cross-plant transfer (five stages: issue → in transit → receipt)
Cross-plant transfer follows a five-stage state machine: once the source plant has issued everything the document becomes "In Transit" and the transfer cost is locked; after the target plant confirms the receipt it becomes posted. Short or over receipts can be force-closed, and the difference automatically creates an adjustment in the source plant. Staff at the target plant query in-transit documents from the "Cross-Plant Receipt" view to take delivery.
Cross-plant transfer screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.

Status | Guide
Draft | Being created; editable.
Confirmed | Effective, waiting for the source plant to issue the stock.
In Transit | Everything has been issued by the source plant and the goods are in transit; it cannot be voided directly.
Posted | The target plant has received everything (or the document was force-closed).
Cancelled | Reverse the issue before receiving.

Cross-plant transfer
1
The source plant creates the document (destination plant, product, quantity) → submit or confirm.
2
Issue from the source plant warehouse (XO); once everything is issued the goods go in transit and the transfer cost is locked.
3
The target plant queries in-transit documents on this screen and receives them (XI); the receipt cost is the locked transfer cost.
4
Everything received posts automatically; a short receipt can be force-closed, and the difference creates an IA adjustment in the source plant.
If dispatch is withdrawn and then confirmed again, the transfer cost is the source plant's unit cost at the time of the new confirmation; the receiving plant takes over that cost, not the cost of the withdrawn dispatch.
Printing
The button on each row of the list (print permission required) opens a printout with a QR code in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. The printout shows the names of both plants and both warehouses; the receiving warehouse name is looked up in the receiving plant's master data.

The three-level storage structure (warehouse / location / lot), the inventory documents, warehouse operations and inventory analysis
The INV (Inventory) module is the core of the stock ledger: every movement is produced through "document → warehouse operation → posting", which writes a stock movement and updates the balance and moving average cost (AVCO; lot-controlled items can use FIFO cost layers) immediately. Documents have three levels (header / line / location detail), separating business confirmation from warehouse execution: the warehouse works location by location under Warehouse Operations, and the document posts automatically once everything is done. The module also covers transfers, stock counts, scrap, loans, samples, outsource and rework material, cross-plant transfers and a range of inventory analysis reports.

Simplified mode (rows on a yellow background) is switched on by a system parameter and suits sites that do not need location-level control; even when simplified, stock movements, cost and journal entries are still produced. A document that has already generated stock movements cannot be withdrawn, only voided (which reverses the movement and the journal entry).

Issues are checked against the available quantity of the location (on hand − reserved) and blocked when it is insufficient.
Posting is subject to the accounting period lock; movements in a closed period are blocked.
A document that has already moved stock cannot be withdrawn by the business side; it can only be voided and reversed.
A receipt whose goods have already been used by later issues cannot be voided directly (from 21 October 2026): for FIFO items, that batch has been consumed; for moving-average items, the void would empty the stock while the value left on the books does not match what would be reversed. Void the issues that used it first, or use a purchase return or stock adjustment instead. Voiding it directly would leave the general-ledger inventory and the stock ledger permanently out of step.
Voiding a document that has already been voided changes nothing.

Route: /LandedCostAllocation | Allocating freight, duty and other import costs into inventory cost
Allocates freight, duty, insurance and other landed costs to receipt lines by amount, quantity or weight, increasing the unit cost of the stock and creating the matching journal entry.
Landed cost allocation screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.

Allocation
1
Click "Add" and choose the receipts to allocate over (more than one is allowed).
2
Enter the cost items and amounts and choose the allocation basis; the system works out how much is allocated to each line.
3
Confirm and post: the inventory cost is updated and the expense journal entry is created.
Only the part still in stock is added to inventory cost: for lines of the same item and location in one allocation, the in-stock ratio is the current on-hand quantity over the total receipt quantity of those lines. That share is capitalized and the rest goes to landed cost variance (5151). When the cost is entered in a foreign currency it is converted to local currency at the buying rate on the document date before it reaches inventory and the ledger; confirmation is blocked if no rate exists, so maintain the rate first.
When the cost invoice arrives
1
On confirmation the cost is first credited to accrued freight (2153).
2
When the freight or duty invoice arrives, create a manual invoice in AP Invoice and choose "2153 accrued freight" as the line account, entering the amount before tax. Posting debits 2153 and credits accounts payable, which clears the accrual.

C.H: Material Staging › Reservation and available quantity
C.T:
Confirming creates, line by line, Hard reservation locks the stock; if any item has too little available the whole document is blocked and stays a draft.
Staging order sourced from a work order : the MRP run has usually already locked stock for the work order, and that portion counts towards the available quantity of this staging order (it is not blocked by the work order's own reservation); once confirmed, the system moves the work order's reservation transferred one for one to the staging order, so the same stock is never locked twice and the available quantity of other work orders is not reduced by mistake. The work order's Material status the quantity locked by the staging order still counts as reserved for that work order, so staging can never make the order look short.
Sourced manually or from an order staging orders do not draw on the work order's reservation and can only use free plant-level stock.
"Void" releases the reservation held by this document and returns the stock to free quantity; where the reservation was transferred from a work order, is not returned to the work order automatically , the work order has to have its material status confirmed again (or MRP re-run) before stock is locked once more.
Picking into the staging warehouse does not release the reservation : the material has only changed location and is still not in production, so the lock has to hold until the issue is posted and only then be released one for one, otherwise a gap opens between staging and issue and another work order could take material that is already prepared.
The reservation is consumed automatically when the issue is posted : posting an issue or return releases this work order's locked quantity one for one, staging order first and work order second; when the work order is completed or voided, any residual lock taken over by the staging order is released with it.
Stock in a staging warehouse still counts toward available quantity : unlike a quarantine warehouse, material in the staging warehouse is already locked by this document's reservation, so excluding it from the available quantity again would deduct the same stock twice and understate the plant's available quantity.

Route: /BatchRelease | Releases a whole batch of work orders into scheduling and dispatch
Release is the gate between planning and execution: the work orders in the batch are released, the system creates dispatches (pulling the machine and tooling requirement from the operations), reserves material at plant level, and puts the work order under schedule freeze protection (an MRP re-run will not move it while it is frozen).
Batch release screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Release
1
Choose a production batch and review the work orders in it and their material status (kitted or at material risk).
2
Confirm and click "Release"; the system creates the dispatches one by one and reserves the material. Work orders that need approval are submitted and can be scheduled and started only after approval. If a work order is above the approval threshold (or meets a mandatory approval condition) but this plant has no work order approval flow, it is approved directly and a reminder lists those work orders so you can check the approval settings.
3
After release, review and adjust the machine assignment under "Production Scheduling".
A work order recalculated to 0 cannot be released : the quantity available at release already covers the gross demand (for example there is enough finished stock), so the recalculated quantity is 0 and nothing needs to be produced. The release is blocked with an explanation; void the work order instead. In a batch release, that work order and the semi-finished child orders under it are skipped, the rest are released as usual, and the result message lists the skipped orders.
A batch is released as a whole, never partly : if any work order in the batch is short of material, nothing is released; if any work order fails during release, nothing is released either. Orders already processed go back to Planned and no approval request is left behind. Fix the cause shown in the message and click Release again.
Stock that covers the demand is held for the original order : the finished goods counted against the demand at release (including the whole quantity when the result is 0) are reserved for the order behind this work order. Other shipments and work orders cannot use them, and the reservation is used up when that order ships. For a semi-finished child order the stock is held for the parent work order and used up when the parent is issued. Work orders entered by hand, not created by MRP, have no source order and reserve nothing.

A dispatch is the execution document at operation level (one operation can be split across several dispatches on different machines). Reporting by barcode from a mobile device is also supported.

2

Starting, reporting and finishing
1
Select a dispatch and click "Start" (the start time is recorded; on a production line several people can start at once). The work order must be Released or In production: a work order still awaiting approval, rejected, or withdrawn back to Planned cannot be started. If the operation has First-piece inspection (FPI) required , and work cannot start until it passes — once staging is done the dispatch stops at "awaiting first piece", and QC first has to Inspection Order "FPI pending registration" (or the first-piece measurement on mobile) has to be passed before it is unlocked. work started directly is still blocked : the gate looks at whether a passing first-piece inspection exists, not at the dispatch's current status, so skipping the staging step does not get round it.
2
During production you can multiple production reports (for example once per transfer batch): enter the good quantity, the defective quantity and the defect reason. After reporting, people stay online and keep producing 。
3
At the end of the session, " Complete (End This Session) ": you can report the final quantity at the same time (leave it blank to just clock out); the system closes the session and settles the labour and overhead cost.
4
If production is not finished you can start again, going round the "start → report → finish" cycle once more; The dispatch closes automatically when the cumulative good quantity reaches the dispatched quantity . On a production line each operator completes and reports their own quantity; the dispatch is closed only when the last person finishes and the quantity target has been met.
5
When the last operation is finished and FQC is required, QA creates the inspection document.
Plants with "Simplified Manufacturing Mode" switched on: A dispatch does not have to be scheduled first — work can start even while it is still "To be scheduled", and such dispatches appear both in the list and in the mobile to-do list. In return, when production is reported the system checks The cumulative quantity completed at an operation cannot exceed that of the previous one (the first operation is exempt), because without a schedule there is nothing to guarantee that earlier operations are done first. The setting is maintained by the system administrator under System Parameters switch; with it off, neither of the two points above applies.
Split dispatch
1
When the quantity has to be produced on more than one machine, use the dispatch panel on Production Schedule and click "Split", entering the quantity and machine for each part; the system creates child dispatches with continued sequence numbers. Only pending or scheduled dispatches can be split.
Handling a dispatch on hold
A dispatch goes on hold automatically in the cases below, and the reason is shown next to its status:
Hold reason | When it happens | How it is released
Machine down | The machine moves to a status where it cannot run, such as breakdown, maintenance or external repair (including the automatic maintenance when tooling reaches its shot limit). Dispatches on that machine that are in setup, ready, pending FPI or in progress all go on hold; dispatches that were only scheduled and not started return to pending and wait to be rescheduled. | They resume automatically when the machine is back to available or standby; for urgent work use "Switch machine".
First-piece inspection failed | The first-piece inspection (FPI) fails. | After the machine is re-adjusted, QC resumes it and the dispatch returns to "Pending FPI" to be measured again.
In-process inspection failed | An in-process inspection (IPQC) of a running dispatch fails. | QC confirms and resumes it, and it goes back to in progress.
A dispatch on hold is not moved by rescheduling and stays on its machine. Click " Handle hold " in the list to open the panel, which offers three ways to deal with it:
1
Resume : the dispatch returns to its status before the hold and continues on the same machine (one held for a failed first piece returns to "Pending FPI"). It cannot resume while the machine is still down. A dispatch held for a quality failure can only be resumed by someone with update permission on inspection orders.
2
Switch machine : pick a machine that can run (machines in the same work center are listed first, and other work centers are allowed). If nothing has been produced, the whole dispatch moves to the new machine; if some has, the original dispatch completes at the quantity done and the remainder goes to a new continuation dispatch (numbered as the original plus -s and a sequence). The continuation returns to "Pending" and needs a new setup and first-piece inspection; rescheduling keeps it on the selected machine . Any session left open on the old machine is closed at the same time and its hours are booked as worked.
3
Close remaining quantity : the remaining quantity will not be produced. If some has been produced the dispatch completes at that quantity; if nothing has, it becomes "Cancelled". This cannot be undone.
When a work order completes automatically: A work order completes automatically only when all its dispatches are "Closed" or "Cancelled" (with at least one closed). A dispatch on hold does not count as finished — its remaining quantity has to be resumed or explicitly closed with "Close remaining quantity".
Printing
The button on each row of the list (print permission required) opens a printout with a QR code in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. The dispatch printout shows the work order, operation, product name, work center and machine names, dispatch quantity and scheduled times, plus the materials list (product code and name, required and issued quantities) to travel with the material to the floor.

Setup time cost: The actual hours for staging (machine setup) are calculated by the system from the start and end times and do not have to be entered. Labour cost per person is counted per person (the person who sets up and the person who produces may not be the same, and their hours are booked separately); overhead is settled over the window from the earliest setup start to setup completion settled only once , and it does not multiply with the number of people doing the setup.

Tooling maintenance: If the tooling used by a dispatch reaches its maintenance threshold in accumulated shots, the status column in the list and the reporting panel show "tooling needs maintenance"; the production report that crosses the threshold automatically creates a machine maintenance downtime document (the machine goes into maintenance and the dispatches already started on it go on hold). Once the maintenance is done an engineer creates an HO event (with the tooling code as the source document number) to bring the machine back and reset the shot count to zero, and the dispatches held because the machine was down resume automatically.

The full production flow, from routing and BOM through the MRP run, scheduling and dispatch, shop-floor reporting and completion receipt
The MFG (Manufacturing) module covers production planning and shop-floor execution: routings define the process and the BOM, and MRP explodes sales orders into work orders and outsource purchase suggestions (for outsource documents see Outsource Management (OSP) module); scheduling and dispatch assign the work to machines, the shop floor reports production from a desktop or a mobile device, and Completion Receipt finally takes the finished goods into stock and works out the work order's actual cost. The module also provides production analysis reports such as work order progress, defect rate, utilisation and OEE.
