C.H: Material Slips › How staging, issue, requisition, backflush and return fit together
C.T:
When a work order is released (MRP explosion / work-order approval) the system places a soft reservation on each material: a plant-level quantity, with no specific location. The material is then consumed by the work order in one of three ways, and anything left over is returned:
Operation | Guide
Staging (optional) | Confirming a staging order transfers the soft reservation to it, then the material is physically moved into the staging area. The reservation stays until the issue is posted. Without staging the soft reservation simply remains.
Issue MI (Push) | Created automatically as a draft when the work order is approved; the warehouse gives the source location and posts it.
Requisition MR (Pull) | Raised by production as needed → submitted → approved by the warehouse → picked and posted. It can be requested straight from the production-session screen on the phone.
Backflush | No slip; material is deducted automatically from the completed quantity when the work order is completed, and remaining reservations are released at closure.
Return MX | Surplus goes back into a chosen location; it cannot exceed what was issued and not yet returned. It comes back at the original issue cost and is no longer reserved for the work order.
Staged material must be taken from the staging location first : whatever is still in the staging area for this work order has to be issued or requisitioned from the staging location; only the shortfall may come from other locations. This is checked when a desktop slip is saved, when the mobile slip is submitted and when it is posted; a violation is blocked with a message saying which location to use and how much. Returns are not affected.

Status | Guide
Draft | Can be edited or deleted. Requisitions (MR) are submitted from here; every other type is simply "Approved".
Pending | Requisitions (MR) only: waiting for warehouse approval.
Approved | Ready to pick.
Picking | The warehouse is picking.
Confirmed | Picking finished; waiting to be posted.
Posted | Stock has moved and the work order's issued/returned totals are updated; it can no longer be changed.
Cancelled | Can be cancelled at any point before posting, including a slip the warehouse has already confirmed as picked (put the picked material back in its original location; nothing has been posted, so stock records are unaffected). Posted or closed slips cannot be cancelled. When the work order is voided, slips from draft up to picking are cancelled automatically. No slip can be posted against a voided work order, and a closed (received) work order accepts returns only — no further issues.

Issue (incl. requisition and outsource issue)
1
Open the slip and, on each line, click the magnifier "Pick from stock" next to "Source Wh/Loc" ; choose one of the locations listed with on-hand and available quantities (warehouse, location and lot are filled in together).
2
Click "Approve" → "Start Picking" → "Confirm Picking" → "Post Issue" in turn. Lines with no source location are reported by line number at posting.
3
Or use "WO Material Issue/Return" on the phone: pick the slip → tap a location → confirm, which picks and posts in one step.
Return
1
Return types show only "Return to Wh/Loc" : give the location the material goes back into (no stock to pick from).
2
Once posted, the material comes back at its original issue cost and the work order's returned quantity goes up.
A return is costed at the weighted average of what is still out on this work order for that item (value issued less value already returned) — not the current stock cost, and not the average of all issues. Returns are still allowed after the work order is closed (leftover material found on the floor), but that material's cost is already in the finished goods, so the system also posts a journal: debit raw material inventory, credit manufacturing cost variance, which keeps the closed work order's WIP at zero.
Printing
The button on each row of the list (print permission required) opens a printout with a QR code in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. The printout shows the category, source document and subcontractor name, and for each line the product code and name, requested/approved/confirmed quantities, unit and from/to warehouse and location, for picking and sign-off.

Slip No | Numbered by the system, with a prefix that depends on the type (MI / MR / MX / OI / OR / RI / RX)
Category | Required Seven business paths: MI in-plant issue (created automatically once the work order is released; for a rework order the automatic slip is RI) / MR in-plant requisition (raised by production as needed, requires approval) / MX in-plant return / OI outsource issue / OR outsource return / RI rework issue / RX rework return. Work order material slips never create journal entries (the material just moves in and out of work in process) and are settled at completion receipt; rework without a work order uses the INV Rework Material document instead
Doc Date | Required Date of the issue or return
Target supplier | For outsource types (OI / OR), the subcontractor receiving the material
Source doc type / Source doc No | Source document that produced this demand, for tracing where it came from. Pick the source doc type from the list (work order; outsource categories can also use an outsource purchase order) and search the source doc No by keyword. Only documents that can still issue or return material are listed: issue categories show released and in-progress work orders, return categories also include completed ones; closed (received into stock) and void ones are not listed. Outsource purchase orders are listed only once confirmed.
Notes | Notes for the whole document
Lines
Field | Guide
Item | Required Item to be issued or returned
Requested qty / Unit | Required Demand quantity and unit of measure. The unit is always the product's stock unit , filled in once the product is chosen — work-order materials, issue/return limits and posting all use the stock unit, and any other unit is rejected on save.

If some of the item is also reserved for orders or work orders, a yellow notice at the top of the window lists it (those reservations are not tied to a location, so "Available" in the table does not deduct them; shipping more than on-hand minus reserved is blocked).
Return to warehouse / Location | Return types only. Where the returned material is put
Lot | Lot for lot-controlled items; it drives traceability and shelf-life control
Status flow: draft → pending (requisitions MR only) → approved → picking → confirmed → posted.

C.H: MRP Run › How the quantity covered from stock is worked out
C.T:
The "covered from stock" figure in the expansion result is not the number on the inventory balance report. What the system may actually use to cover demand is:
usable = max( available stock + in-transit approved POs + goods awaiting put-away − shipments awaiting picking − safety stock , 0 )
Term | Guide
Safety stock | The product master's safety stock is deducted first; MRP never draws on it . Seeing a requisition or work order raised while stock appears to be on hand is therefore normal — the gap is usually exactly this
In-transit approved POs | Counts only the undelivered quantity of purchase orders that are approved , still open, and due on or before the required date . Draft or pending POs, and POs due later than the required date, do not count
Awaiting put-away / awaiting picking | Full mode only. Goods received but not yet put away have not increased stock, so they are added back; shipments confirmed but not yet picked have not decreased it, so they are deducted. In simplified mode approval posts immediately, stock is already up to date, and neither adjustment is made
Where several levels of one explosion need the same item, in-transit and awaiting-put-away quantities are claimed only once and never counted twice. They are drawn in a fixed order — on-hand, then in-transit POs, then goods awaiting put-away — and the on-hand portion alone may not fall below safety stock either.

C.H: MRP Run › Decimals of the material demand quantity (from 2026-07)
C.T:
1
When a lower level is exploded, demand = parent quantity × usage per unit × (1 + offcut rate% + scrap rate%), which can produce a decimal (e.g. 105 × 1.05 = 110.25).
2
The system uses the material's rounded up to the decimals of the unit of measure : PCS has 0 decimals, so 110.25 rounds up to 111 ; if the unit allows 4 decimals, 110.25 is kept as it is. If the unit is not found in the unit-of-measure master the value is kept unchanged, without rounding up.
3
only affects work orders exploded after that, the demand quantity of existing work orders is not changed retroactively ; an older work order has to have MRP re-run to move onto the new basis. You can check under WO Material Status Review the actual demand and the shortfall.
Plants with "Simplified Manufacturing Mode" switched on: do not need to create a run here by hand — approving a sales order automatically creates an MRP run, explodes it immediately and then releases the work orders. The message shown after saving tells you the run number that was created. The system only covers the quantity that has not been exploded yet, so saving the same order again does not explode it twice. If the automatic run fails the message explains why and the run stays in Draft status, which can be viewed here and carried out by hand. The setting is maintained by the system administrator under System Parameters switch.

Route: /MrpVarianceDecision | List of the gaps between existing purchase requisitions and the latest MRP run
Re-running MRP deletes and rebuilds work orders that have not been released, but Purchase requisitions already submitted or approved are not overwritten automatically — approved documents are governed by the approval flow and MRP cannot take them back. The two sides can therefore drift apart; the classic case is an item switched from "buy" to "make" and then re-run: the demand has moved to a work order, but the original purchase requisition is still sitting there.
This list turns such gaps into outstanding items that have to be cleared , which stay on the list until they have been dealt with instead of flashing up a single message at the moment of the re-run.
MRP reconciliation decision screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Type | Meaning
Switched to make/outsource | The purchase is no longer needed and the same run produced a work order for the item — the demand has simply moved to another supply route. The notes column shows the work order that has taken it over.
Demand removed | The purchase is no longer needed and there is no matching work order either (the order was cut back, for example).
Increase / decrease | The item still has to be purchased but the quantity has changed. Approved purchase requisitions are not re-quantified automatically.
Add | A newly added purchase requirement; the existing requisition has already moved on and cannot take it, so a separate requisition is needed.

1
Close & retire : tick the items marked "switched to make or outsource" or "demand gone" and click it; the system marks the matching requisition lines as closed so they are never converted to a purchase. does not delete the document , and the approval trail is kept in full.
2
Mark handled : items that cannot be handled automatically — already converted to a purchase, or in approval — should be dealt with on the requisition or purchase order first and then marked here, so that the to-do list does not pile up.
Safeguards: The variance list is a snapshot taken when MRP was re-run. When you click "Close and drop", the system re-checks every as it stands — lines that have since been converted to a purchase, or whose requisition is in approval, are skipped automatically and listed in the result message, so nothing is closed by mistake.

C.H: MRP Variance Decisions › Automatic closing (system parameter)
C.T: System Parameters mfg_mrp_auto_close_obsolete_pr Set to true is on, the re-run automatically closes lines that were never converted to a purchase and are no longer needed, so they do not have to be handled from this list; such items are kept with the status "closed automatically" for traceability. It is off by default (the system only prompts and someone confirms).

Route: /Oee | OEE = Availability × Performance × Quality
Calculates OEE the standard way: Availability (actual run time / planned time, planned time taken from the work calendar shift hours) × Performance (ideal time / run time, where ideal time = output × standard UnitTime) × Quality (good pieces / total output). The three factors can be broken down by machine and period to find the biggest source of loss.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Machine | One machine only; leave blank for all machines

Report fields
Field | Guide
Machine / Item | Machine and produced item in the statistics
Planned (min) | Planned production minutes from the work calendar (regular + overtime), the denominator of availability
Run (min) | Minutes the machine was actually running
Ideal (min) | Total output × standard unit time, i.e. the minutes it would take with no loss at all
Total output / Good | Total output in the period and the good pieces within it
Availability | Run hours ÷ planned hours, showing how much of the planned time the machine was really running
Performance | Ideal hours ÷ run hours, showing whether the speed during running met the standard
Yield | Good pieces ÷ total output, a measure of output quality
OEE | Availability × Performance × Quality. Each ratio is capped at 100% so that noisy data does not distort the result

Route: /ProductionCompletion | Receiving finished goods into stock and carrying the work order's actual cost forward
Receives output that has finished the last operation and passed FQC into the finished goods warehouse. Posting creates the INV receipt movement together with the labour and overhead absorption entries, establishes the work order's actual cost (preliminary), and completes the work order automatically once the received quantity reaches the work order quantity. Rework work orders can be received down three routes: good pieces (finished goods warehouse), downgraded pieces (seconds warehouse, cost written down) and scrap. Good units from a rework order are received only at the original value of the defective items issued in; the extra material, labour and overhead spent on the rework go to "5250 Rework Loss" (see Rework cost on the WO Cost Variance page ).
Completion receipt screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.

Status | Guide
Draft | Created but not yet effective; can be freely edited or deleted, and submitted for approval from this status.
Pending approval | Submitted and waiting for approval; it cannot be edited, but it can be withdrawn back to draft.
Confirmed | Effective once approved (or confirmed directly when no approval is required), waiting for the next step or for posting.
Posted | Stock and accounting have been posted; the document can no longer be changed.
Void | Reverses what was posted; the void reason is kept and the action cannot be undone.

Receive into stock
1
Click "Add" and choose a work order; the system fills in the quantity available to receive (completed − already received − awaiting inspection).
2
Enter the quantity to receive and the receiving warehouse and location, then save and confirm.
3
Once confirmed and posted the stock is booked in, and the work order completes automatically when the cumulative received quantity reaches the target.
Fully outsourced work orders do not go through production completion. Their finished goods are stocked by the outsource receipt (cost = processing fee + materials sent out), and the order becomes "Received into stock" automatically once the returned goods have passed and been stocked in full; running completion on it here is refused, so the same goods cannot be stocked twice.
Work orders with an outsourced operation: the outsource cost accumulated at receipt (processing fee + materials consumed) is included in the finished goods' unit cost on receipt into stock and recorded as "Actual Outsource Cost" in the work order's actual cost; it is not part of the labour/overhead absorption entry (the fee was already posted to inventory at the outsource receipt).
Finished output is held for the original order : when a work order created by MRP is received into stock, its output is reserved for the order behind it (for a semi-finished item, for the parent work order), up to the demand quantity; anything above that is free stock.

Confirmation fields
Field | Guide
Work Order No | Work order being received, read-only
Item | Finished item being received, read-only
Completed quantity | Good quantity being received this time, read-only (taken from the cumulative production reports)
Warehouse | Required Warehouse the finished goods go into
Receipt location | Required Location the finished goods go into; the warehouse's default location is filled in
Lot | Lot for lot-controlled items; left blank, the system generates it from the numbering rule and works out the expiry from the product's shelf life
Receive by box | When ticked, the completed quantity is received as several boxes of the "quantity per box", one lot per box (see "Receiving by box and box labels" below); the "Lot" field then becomes the lot prefix
Container | Container type used for the boxes; is prefilled with the last operation's output container. Choosing another container replaces the quantity per box with that container's maximum capacity. It is only printed on the box labels and does not affect inventory
Quantity per box | Required when boxing How many go into each box (stock unit); is prefilled with the container's maximum capacity. The screen shows straight away how many boxes there will be and how many the last box holds
Box numbers (optional) | The boxes to fill, one per line in box order; scan them or click "Fill in empty boxes". The count must equal the number of boxes, and each box lot is linked to its box number
Receiving by box and box labels
1
In the confirmation panel tick "Receive by box" and check the container and quantity per box.
2
Enter a lot prefix in "Lot"; if it is blank, the work order number is used. Each box's lot is the prefix + "-" + the box number. For example, 100 pieces at 30 per box give PREFIX-01 to PREFIX-03 with 30 each and PREFIX-04 with the remaining 10. With 100 boxes or more the box number has three digits ( -001 ), so sorting the lots as text keeps them in box order.
3
(Optional) If your boxes carry fixed QR labels and are reused, scan the boxes to fill into the "Box numbers" field in order, one per line, or click "Fill in empty boxes" to fill in empty boxes of that container. The number of box numbers must equal the number of boxes; on receipt, box 1's lot is linked to the first box number, and so on. If any box does not exist, is inactive, belongs to another container type or still holds goods, nothing is received. Leave it blank to skip linking boxes.
4
Click "Confirm receipt". If you entered box numbers , each box already carries its fixed QR label (printed beforehand on the Boxes screen, no need to wait until it is filled); scanning it brings up the box's current lot and quantity, so no extra label is printed after receipt. If you did not enter box numbers , the panel shows "Print box labels" when it succeeds, one label per box; the QR code on each label is that box's lot, so scanning the label later is the same as entering that box's lot.
Box lots must not repeat an existing lot. If the item has ever used any of the box lots (including one that has since been cleared to zero), nothing is received; use another prefix and receive again. The same item and lot merge into one balance, so that box could no longer be told apart. At most 999 boxes can be received at once; more than that usually means the quantity per box was mistyped.
Boxing only changes which lots the goods are received under: every box has the same unit cost, and the total quantity and cost received are exactly the same as without boxing. This is the "one lot per box" approach, so a box cannot hold more than one item or lot; to reuse boxes, link the lots to boxes as in step 3 above.
Backflushed material is deducted automatically at completion, based on the quantity actually finished, with no separate issue slip; where the inspection rule has "FQC required on completion" ticked, the final inspection must be passed before stock can be received.
Where backflushed material is deducted from
1
Backflush does not go through a staging order, so there is no field anywhere to enter the source location ; the system decides it.
2
It first takes the default warehouse and default location of the product category that the material belongs to (the same convention as receipt put-away) and checks that they are usable in the current plant.
3
Where the product category has nothing set, or has a warehouse but no location, it falls back to the warehouse and location entered for this completion receipt .
Set the product category defaults before you split warehouses ( Product Category ). While raw material and finished goods share one warehouse, steps 2 and 3 give the same answer and nothing shows. Once finished goods get their own warehouse, the finished-goods location holds no raw material, so the backflush is rejected by the issue check for insufficient quantity — and because the backflush and the receipt sit in one transaction , the whole work order cannot be received , with a message that only says stock is short and never points at the setting.

Work Orders 、 MRP Run
An operation's move time and queue time are the time between this operation finishing and the next one starting ; they affect the start dates MRP works back to and the gaps the scheduler leaves between operations. Every night at 02:00 the system works out a suggested queue time from the last 90 days of production reports: the gap from the previous operation's last clock-out to the next operation's first clock-in on the same work order, counting only working time on the work calendar (nights, holidays and breaks are excluded), taking the median and deducting this operation's move time. Nothing is calculated before the first operation, and there is no suggestion with fewer than 5 samples. When you edit an operation, the queue time field shows "Suggested X (median of N actual reports over the last 90 days)"; clicking "Apply" only fills in the field, and it takes effect only when you save the routing — the system never changes routings by itself.
Note: Changing a routing does not update existing work orders; to change the process on a work order that has been released, void it and open a new one.

Route: /Schedule | Machine Gantt scheduling with conflict warnings
Shows the dispatches on each machine as a Gantt chart and supports rescheduling. The scheduling engine lays work out on the work calendar and shift pattern (genuinely available time); frozen (released) work orders are not moved by a reschedule. Material risk and tooling conflicts (the same tooling claimed by more than one machine in the same period) are marked by colour but not blocked — see "Gantt chart colours" below.
Production scheduling screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Scheduling actions
1
Choose a date range to load the Gantt chart and see the load and queue on each machine.
2
The bar at the top shows whether the schedule is out of date (any release, split, machine switch, completion, cancellation, machine status change, work calendar or planned downtime change since the last run makes it out of date, and the bar says since when), the time and trigger of the last run, the number of pending and on-hold dispatches, and this plant's automatic rescheduling settings (including the sequencing rule and freeze window). The bar turns yellow when the schedule is out of date.
3
Click "Run Schedule" to have the engine re-lay pending and scheduled dispatches. Before it runs, you are told how many scheduled dispatches will be re-laid and how many of them are tomorrow's (the floor may already have staged or set up for them from the preparation alert), and it runs only after you confirm. Dispatches in setup, ready, pending FPI, in progress or on hold are not moved. A machine chosen when reassigning, splitting or switching machine is kept, and the dispatch moves to another machine only if that one cannot run. Only one scheduling run per plant can be in progress at a time; if someone else is running it you are asked to try again shortly. If a dispatch is changed during the run (by a production report, for example), nothing is saved and you simply run it again. If you see "Scheduling could not finish within 90 days… Check that the work calendar is set up.", a work center or machine that a dispatch needs has no usable work calendar (for example, no shift group); nothing is saved, so set up the calendar and run it again.
4
Check the orange (material risk), purple (tooling conflict) and red (predicted late) marks and adjust by hand where necessary.
5
Once the schedule is settled, each dispatch's ETA is written back as the work order's estimated completion date.

By default the schedule is only updated when someone clicks "Run Schedule". Under System Parameters → Manufacturing Settings (or each plant's plant parameters ) you can turn on three kinds of automatic rescheduling, which can be combined:
When | How it works
After changes | The system checks every minute whether the schedule is out of date; when it is and the last change was 90 seconds ago, it re-runs. If changes keep coming (continuous production reporting, for example), it re-runs after at most 10 minutes anyway.
Before dispatch | When Dispatch Operations is searched, the mobile dispatch list or the Preparation Board (desktop and mobile) or this screen is opened, and before the 17:00 preparation alert is sent, an out-of-date schedule is re-run first, so the page appears a few seconds later. If the re-run fails, the page still shows the existing schedule.
Daily | A full re-run once a day at the set time, whether or not the schedule is out of date; set it before the 17:00 preparation alert. If the server was off at that time it runs once it is back the same day, and it never runs twice on one day.
Sequencing rule and freeze window
1
Sequencing rule : automatic runs sequence production batches by the "Sequencing rule for automatic runs" system parameter, Priority when it is not set. The rule selector on this screen defaults to the same rule, so a manual run does not accidentally undo an automatic run with a different rule; you can still pick another when you need to.
2
Freeze window : when set, scheduled dispatches starting within that many hours keep their machine and time slot in automatic runs, just like dispatches already under way — the shop floor may already be staging material and tooling for them. Rush orders go after them. Dispatches on a machine that can no longer run, or whose whole slot has passed without starting, are rescheduled as usual.
3
The freeze window only applies to automatic runs ; clicking "Run Schedule" gives the planner full control, and dispatches inside the window can move. Note also that if a dispatch inside the window is cancelled or finishes early, the gap it leaves is only filled once the window has passed.
Automatic runs work like manual ones: dispatches in setup, ready, pending FPI, in progress or on hold stay where they are, and machines chosen by people are kept. If an automatic run after 17:00 changes the machine or time of any of tomorrow's dispatches , a "tomorrow's dispatches changed" notification goes to the same role as the preparation alert; check staging and setup on the Preparation Board .
How planned times follow progress
Even without rescheduling, planned dispatch times follow shop-floor progress, in two layers:
1
After each production report : the dispatch's expected finish is recalculated from the remaining quantity, and the following dispatches on the same machine, the later operations of the same work order and the parent work order's dispatches are shifted with it — only those within the next 48 hours, at most 50, so reporting stays fast. If a production batch becomes predicted late as a result, people with access to Production Schedule get a notification.
2
Nightly calibration at 01:00 : covers what lies beyond 48 hours, and uses the same rules as Run Schedule to calculate times (operation overlap, work calendar, planned downtime, started dispatches re-estimated from their remaining quantity): when earlier work runs late, later work moves later; when it finishes early, later work moves earlier; and dispatches whose start has passed without starting move to now. The only difference is that it does not change machines, change the order, or place pending dispatches — that is rescheduling, which follows each plant's automatic rescheduling settings or a manual run. Afterwards each production batch is re-checked for predicted lateness, and newly late batches are notified to production planning.

The "Run History" tab lists every schedule run, manual or automatic, for 60 days. Once automatic rescheduling is on, nobody clicks Run Schedule by hand any more, so this is where you see why dispatches moved.
The Run History tab: one row per run at the top; click a row to list that run's dispatch changes underneath
Column | Meaning
Run at, Trigger, Rule | When the run happened, who started it or which automatic trigger did (after changes / before dispatch / daily), and which sequencing rule it used.
Scheduled | Dispatches given a slot in this run, including ones whose slot did not change.
Newly scheduled / Time changed / Machine changed / Back to pending | Dispatches that actually changed compared with before the run: pending ones now placed, ones whose start moved on the same machine, ones moved to another machine, and scheduled ones that could not be placed and went back to pending.
Affects tomorrow | How many of those changes were, or now are, on tomorrow; shown in red when above 0 — check staging and setup on the Preparation Board.
Kept by freeze window | Dispatches kept in place by the freeze window; "—" for runs without one.
Click a row to list each dispatch that changed in that run (work order, operation, old machine and start, new machine and start). If a run changed more than 1,000 dispatches only the first 1,000 are listed; the counts above still cover all of them. The 01:00 nightly calibration does not change machines or order and is not recorded here.

Colour by
The "Colour By" selector above the chart switches between two ways of colouring, and reloads the data when you change it:
1
Status (default): colours each dispatch by its current condition, so the ones needing attention stand out.
2

A dispatch only ever carries one colour. When more than one condition applies, the first match from the top of this table wins — a dispatch already in progress stays green even if it is late, and the lateness is called out in the tooltip instead.

The judgement is made per batch, so every dispatch in that batch turns red, not only the one that overran. Back-scheduling automatically skips non-working days; gaps in the calendar push the schedule onto the wrong dates, so confirm the whole year's calendar before going live.
After changing overtime hours, the available time for that month has to be rebuilt before the scheduler can see them. When you edit a day's overtime here (or move its date, shift pattern, work center or machine), the rebuild happens automatically and takes effect on save; nothing else is needed. However, calendars generated before this feature existed still carry the old regular-time-only segments — run Batch Generate once for that year and month. Even without ticking "Overwrite existing on regenerate" the available time is rebuilt, while the existing calendar rows and any overtime you adjusted are kept exactly as they are and are never reset to the shift pattern's defaults.

Route: /WorkOrderMaterialStatus | Demand, issue and shortage by material for a work order
Lists demand, issued, returned, net issued, unissued and plant-level available quantity for every material by work order × operation × BOM sequence, together with its kitting status. When a production batch is blocked from release by a shortage, this is where you find out which work order, which material and how much is missing.
Work order material status screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Can be filtered by production batch, work order number and item; tick "show incomplete kits only" to see just the material that is short or waiting for a lower level to finish.
2
The cards at the top show the number of material lines, shortage lines, lines waiting for a lower level to finish and lines with material still unissued.
3
Export to Excel is supported (print permission required).

Demand / Issued / Returned : taken from the work order material, in the issuing unit. Net Issued = issued − returned; Unissued qty = demand − net issued (never below 0).
Available = plant on hand − active on-hand reservations (quarantine warehouses excluded) + the work order's own reservation , on the same basis as the material gate in batch release. The MRP run locks on-hand stock for the work order, and because that reservation is held for this work order it counts as covered when deciding whether the work order is fully staged; quantities locked by Other Quantities locked by documents are still deducted as usual. The work order's Material Staging the quantity it has locked also counts as "its own" — the work order's reservation was transferred to it when the staging was confirmed.
Kitting status ：
Ready Enough is available, or the line is backflushed (deducted at completion), or the lower-level work order is already finished.
Shortage Available is less than demand.
Pending Sub-assembly The material comes from a lower-level work order which has not finished yet.
Backflushed material and lower-level made items are not checked against stock, so the available column shows "—".
This screen is a read-only enquiry and does not change the work order's material status; to refresh the material badge on the work order header, open the work order and click "Check material".

C.H: WO Material Status › Quantity display and decimals
C.T:
The quantity defaults to the material's Unit of measure decimals is displayed (PCS has 0 decimals, so a whole number is shown).
but the scrap rate and offcut rate can produce a requirement with more decimals than the unit allows (e.g. 105 × 1.05 = 110.25 while PCS has 0 decimals). In that case shows the true value without rounding , so you never get the confusing case of "demand 110, available 110, yet marked short".
Rows judged short of material carry a note under the available quantity Short by the shortfall (e.g. "0.25 short"), i.e. the actual gap between demand and available quantity.
From 2026-07 : when the MRP run creates the work order material, the demand is rounded to the decimals of that material's unit of measure rounded up (PCS has 0 decimals, so 110.25 rounds up to 111), so that a whole-number unit never carries a fractional demand. The adjustment only affects work orders exploded afterwards; the demand quantity of existing work orders is not changed retroactively , to move an older work order onto the new basis, re-run its MRP Run . If the unit is not found in the unit-of-measure master the value is kept as it is, without rounding up.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Batch / Work order No / Item | each narrows the query scope
Show shortages only | Lists only items that are not fully staged (unissued quantity greater than available)
List columns
Field | Guide
Batch / Work order No / Status | The production batch and work order the material status belongs to, and the work order's current status
Output | Finished or semi-finished item the work order produces
Operation | Routing operation the material belongs to
Item code / Item name | Item to be issued
Issue Method | Issue (a slip is raised by hand) or backflush (deducted automatically at completion according to the usage)
Demand qty | Quantity that should be issued, calculated from the work order quantity and the BOM usage (including scrap rate and offcut rate)
Issued / Returned | Cumulative quantity actually issued and returned
Net Issued | Issued − returned, i.e. the quantity actually on the line now
Unissued qty | Demand − net issued, i.e. what is still to be issued
Available | Available stock of the item at the moment (other documents' reservations already deducted)
Kitting status | The unissued quantity compared with the available quantity; too little available counts as a shortage and blocks release

Route: /WorkOrderVariance | Standard vs actual cost variance analysis for work orders (material, efficiency and rate variance)
Compares the actual cost of a work order (material, labour, overhead) with standard and breaks the difference into usage, efficiency and rate variance. After the actual rates are re-estimated at month end, the variance is restated through an adjusting journal entry (preliminary → final).
Work order cost variance screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

C.H: WO Cost Variance › Where actual cost comes from
C.T:
This screen is the main place to look up a work order's actual cost. Actual cost is not available at all times: it is created and then finalised at two specific points in the work order's life cycle.
Point in time | Status | What happens
Work order closed | Preliminary | When production is put away and the work order is closed, the system settles one actual-cost record: issued material, reported labour and overhead are written in and compared with standard to derive the variance. At this stage labour and overhead still use estimated rates .
Month-end rate re-estimate | Final | Once the month-end run performs the actual rate re-estimate, labour and overhead are recalculated from that period's departmental actual costs, the difference is restated through an adjusting journal entry, and the status becomes "Final".
Two situations make actual cost look "missing", and neither is a fault:
(1) The work order is not closed yet — work orders still in production have no row at all on this screen. For cost still in progress, use the WIP report instead.
(2) The month end has not re-estimated that period yet — the rows are there but the status reads "Preliminary", meaning labour and overhead will still change. Before treating the figures as settled (quoting, performance review, accounting analysis), check that the status is "Final".

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.
2
Can be filtered by work order, item and period; click a row to expand the cost element detail.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
WO No. / Product | Keyword (partial match)
Settlement date from / to | Filters by the work order cost settlement date range
WO Type | Normal / Rework / Outsource; leave blank for all. Exports apply the same filter
Report fields
Field | Guide
WO No. / Product | Settled work orders and the items they produce
WO Type | Shown under the work order number: Rework (yellow) / Outsource; normal work orders carry no tag
Planned qty | Planned output quantity of the work order
Cost Date | Date the work order's actual cost was settled
Material / Labour / Overhead | Standard cost, actual cost and variance for each of the three cost elements; variance = actual − standard, a positive figure meaning over-consumption
Total Variance | Sum of the three element variances, i.e. the overall cost overrun or saving on the work order
Rework Loss | Rework work orders only: the part of the actual total cost above the original value of the defective items issued in, which did not go back to inventory but was charged to 5250 Rework Loss (see "Rework cost" below). Later month-end rate re-estimate differences go to manufacturing cost variance as for any work order and do not change this column
Status | Settlement status. Preliminary = settled at work order close using estimated rates, so labour and overhead will still change; Final = the period's actual rate re-estimate is done and the figures are settled. Always read this column before interpreting the amounts

The cost of a rework work order is a quality failure cost and is reported separately from normal production. At completion receipt:
1
Good units go back to inventory at the original value of the defective items issued into the rework order (their book cost when issued), capped at the actual total cost. Defective items rejected during production that were never received into stock are not on the books, so their original value is 0: their material cost was already spread over the original order's good units.
2
Everything else (extra material, labour, overhead, outsourcing) is debited to "5250 Rework Loss" and does not go into inventory.
When the results include rework work orders, a line below the table shows how many there are, their total actual cost and how much of it is rework loss.

Production Putaway 、 WIP Report 、 Month-End Close 、 Department Actual Cost
Common causes of an unusual variance: an inaccurate standard BOM usage, unreported production hours, or a work center rate that has not been updated.

Route: /WorkOrder | Work order creation, maintenance and lifecycle management
The work order is the central document of production: it records the item to be made, the quantity, the operations (snapshotted from the routing) and the material. There are three types — normal, rework (which needs a source work order) and outsource. Releasing a work order creates dispatches; once production has been reported and FQC passed, the output is received through Completion Receipt, and the work order finishes automatically when everything has been received.
Work order enquiry screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.
2
Can be filtered by status, item, order number and planned start date range.

Status | Guide
Planned | Initial status after MRP conversion or manual creation; still editable.
Released | Released through batch release, which creates the dispatches; while frozen it is not moved by an MRP reschedule.
In production | production has already been reported.
Completed | The work order completes automatically when all its dispatches are closed or cancelled (with at least one closed). A dispatch on hold does not count as finished: its remaining quantity has to be resumed or ended with "Close remaining quantity" on Dispatch Operations. The cost is carried into the work order's actual cost.
Cancelled | Production is cancelled and any reserved material is released automatically. Unfinished dispatches become "Cancelled" at the same time, so they leave the shop-floor list and no longer take up scheduling capacity.
Fully outsourced work orders: each time returned goods pass inspection and enter stock the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity grows, and once full the order goes straight from "In progress" to "Received into stock" (no "Completed" step, no production completion).

Create a work order by hand
1
Click "Add", then choose the item (the routing is filled in automatically), the quantity and the planned completion date.
2
Rework orders: in the list, click Create Rework on a work order that is Completed or Closed enter the rework quantity, and under Operations to redo tick only the operations that must be redone (all are ticked by default; at least one is required). The system creates a work order of type Rework linked to the original, keeping its batch and routing and copying only the ticked operations and the materials under them; the materials are scaled by rework quantity ÷ original quantity and the issued quantities start at 0. When the defective items are in stock (for example rejected after being received), tick The defective items are in stock : a material line for the defective item itself is added, issued with the rework issue on release, and at completion the good units go back to inventory at its book value. It is ticked by default for a Closed (received) work order and unticked for a Completed one that has not been received — defective items rejected during production are not on the books, and ticking it would make the warehouse issue good units from stock as if they were the defective ones. A rework order created by executing an NCR rework disposition follows the same rules but takes all operations (there is nothing to tick when executing); if only some operations need redoing, create the rework from Create Rework in the work order list instead. On release, the slip created automatically for Push materials is a rework issue (RI) , not an ordinary in-plant issue. Material issued to and returned from a rework order creates no journal entry; the original value and the rework loss are settled at completion receipt (see Rework cost ).
3
Once saved, it is released through the release process.
4
If the release is waiting for approval, click "Withdraw" in the detail panel to cancel the submission: the work order goes back to Planned and its approval status to draft, so you can edit it and release it again. When the approval is rejected or returned for revision , the work order also goes back to Planned automatically; correct it and release it again to resubmit. Which work orders are submitted: with a work order approval flow, those whose standard cost is above the plant's amount threshold (every order if no threshold is set); outsourced, rework or delayed orders are always submitted when the corresponding mandatory condition is on. If an order meets these conditions but the plant has no work order approval flow , it is approved directly and a reminder pops up — please check the approval settings. A work order that is awaiting approval or was rejected is not scheduled and cannot be started — production begins only after approval. When it goes back to Planned (withdrawn or rejected), dispatches that were scheduled but not started return to "Pending scheduling" and are scheduled again after the next release.
5
To drop a work order you no longer need, click "Void" in the detail panel: its open dispatches are cancelled and reserved materials released. It is blocked, with the reason shown, if anything has been produced or issued materials have not been returned — return the materials first. Unposted issue slips: those from draft up to picking are cancelled automatically with the void; an issue slip the warehouse has already confirmed as picked blocks the void (have the warehouse cancel it and put the material back, or post it and then return the materials with a return slip). A work order already converted to an outsource purchase order is blocked too: delete a draft outsource PO first; void a confirmed one on Outsource Purchase Orders first (only before any receipt and once materials at the vendor are returned). Once a work order is voided, any leftover issue slip or outsource receipt for it can no longer be posted. Closed or voided work orders have no Void button.
A work order recalculated to 0 cannot be released : the quantity available at release already covers the gross demand (for example there is enough finished stock), so the recalculated quantity is 0 and nothing needs to be produced. The release is blocked with an explanation; void the work order instead. In a batch release, that work order and the semi-finished child orders under it are skipped, the rest are released as usual, and the result message lists the skipped orders.
Stock that covers the demand is held for the original order : the finished goods counted against the demand at release (including the whole quantity when the result is 0) are reserved for the order behind this work order. Other shipments and work orders cannot use them, and the reservation is used up when that order ships. For a semi-finished child order the stock is held for the parent work order and used up when the parent is issued. Work orders entered by hand, not created by MRP, have no source order and reserve nothing.
Printing
The work order printout is meant for the shop floor: it shows the header, the routing and the materials to issue for each operation — product code and name, required, issued and returned quantities, quantity still to issue (required − issued + returned), unit and issue method; backflushed materials are deducted automatically at completion, so the quantity to issue does not apply. Costs are not printed (see standard and actual costs on screen).

Header
Field | Guide
Work Order No | Numbered by the system; not editable
Item | Finished or semi-finished item this work order produces
Count | Planned output; MRP works the release quantity back from the cumulative yield
Status | Progress of the work order (planned / released / in production / completed / settled)
Operations
Field | Guide
Seq | Order in which the operations run
Operation / Work center | Operation name and the work center that performs it
Setup | Setup time such as changing tooling or lines, counted once per dispatch
Unit Time | Standard time needed to produce one good piece
Outsource | Marks whether the operation is subcontracted to an outside supplier
Materials | The material list exploded from the BOM for this operation
Cost fields
Field | Guide
Material / Labour / Manufacturing overhead | The three cost elements, each shown as standard and actual
Standard | Cost that should have been consumed, calculated from the standard usage and the standard rate
Actual | Cumulative material, labour and overhead actually put in; the variance appears once the work order is settled, and the period-end actual rate re-estimate may adjust it again

Batch Release 、 Dispatch Operations 、 Production Putaway 、 WO Cost Variance
The work order screen shows the kitting status (MaterialRisk); where material is short but the in-transit quantity is expected before the start date, it is marked yellow as a material risk.
Note: The system decides when a work order is finished from the quantity received into stock; do not force it closed by hand and then receive the rest afterwards.

Path: /mobile/approval/list.html | Seeing and approving the documents that are waiting for you, on a phone
Tap "My Approvals" on the home page. The number on the tile is how many documents are waiting for you right now, and no number is shown when there are none. This entry point does not need a mobile module permission — what you see is decided entirely by who the approval flow says the approver for this step is, and it is the same list as "My Pending Approvals" on the desktop.
The approval list (shown here in its empty state, "Nothing is waiting for your approval"; when there is something, each document gets its own card — the fields are listed below)

C.H: My Approvals (Mobile) › What the list shows
C.T:
Field | Notes
Document type (grey badge) | The document type name in the interface language, such as "Purchase Request" or "Work Order". It comes from the same list as the desktop pending list , so a document is named the same on the computer and the phone.
Step N | Which step of the approval flow the document is sitting at.
Document number | The largest line on the card.
Requester · date | Who submitted it and when.
The list only shows documents in your current plant . Switching plant switches the list too — see "Switching plant" in the mobile overview .

1
Tap "Review and approve" on the card and the "For approval" dialog opens.
2
Check the amount , plant and the header fields at the top (supplier, customer, required date and so on); "Lines" below lists the items and quantities.
3
Tap "Open in desktop app" when you need the whole document; it opens the desktop screen in a new tab (the mobile summary is a summary by design).
4
Type anything you want to say in "Comment (optional)" , or leave it blank.
5
Tap "Approve" or "Reject" and confirm. The list reloads itself afterwards and the document is gone from it.
The phone offers only Approve and Reject ; the desktop's "Return for revision" is not available . Use the desktop when you want the requester to amend and resubmit: a rejection ends the flow, whereas returning it keeps the flow open, and the outcomes are not the same.

C.H: My Approvals (Mobile) › Reading the "For approval" dialog
C.T:
Area | Notes
Amount | The large figure at the top, with its currency. Document types that have no amount at all (a purchase request or a work order, for example) show "No amount for this document type" — that is not the same thing as an amount of zero, and the screen deliberately keeps them apart.
Plant and header fields | Each document type decides which header fields to show, and the ones chosen are those you cannot sensibly approve without.
Lines | Item, quantity with its unit, and amount. On a long document only the first few lines are shown and the dialog says "N more line(s) not shown" at the bottom; open the desktop app for the full list.
The summary exists so that you can make the decision on a phone ; it is not the complete document. For large amounts, or when the lines are truncated, open it on the desktop before you decide.

C.H: My Approvals (Mobile) › Which document types can be approved on mobile
C.T:
There are 14 document types that can be approved on the phone today:
Module | Document types
Purchasing (PUR) | Purchase Request, Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Goods Return, Outsource Receipt, Vendor Evaluation
Orders (ORD) | Sales Order, Goods Shipment, Sales Return, Internal Order
Manufacturing (MFG) | Work Order
Quality (QCR) | Non-Conformance Report
Finance (FIN) | AP Invoice, AR Invoice
The remaining types are visible but cannot be approved on the phone. The card says "This document type cannot be approved on mobile yet; please use the desktop app" and offers a desktop link. This is a deliberate limitation, not a fault:
Kind | Why not on mobile
Master data changes
Company , Product , Tax | These are not transactions: there is no amount and no line detail, so a summary would say no more than the list already does.
Warehouse documents
Scrap, loan, sample, stock adjustment, transfer, cross-plant transfer, outsource material, rework material, staging order, landed cost allocation | The decision rests on the physical stock and its locations (or on a whole variance sheet, or allocation ratios); an item-and-quantity summary is not enough to support it. Putting an approve button on the phone would be inviting blind approval.
When a type has no desktop document link registered either, the card says "No document link is registered for this type; please use the desktop app" — it tells you, rather than silently doing nothing.

C.H: My Approvals (Mobile) › No connection and state changes
C.T:
Approvals are never queued. Tapping approve or reject with no connection shows "No connection. Approvals are never queued for later — please wait until the connection is back." straight away. This differs from production reporting or stock counting: those record something that happened on the floor and a few minutes' delay changes nothing, whereas an approval is a decision made now, and queuing it would delay its effect without the approver knowing.
If the document is withdrawn, or handled by another approver while your dialog is open, the submission is rejected with an explanation and the list reloads — what you then see is the list as it stands now, not the one you opened.
When the document no longer exists, or is not in your current plant, the dialog says "This document no longer exists, or is not in your current plant." and offers no approve or reject buttons — if you cannot see it, you cannot sign it .

Mobile and desktop share the same pending list : sign on either one and the other loses that document. The desktop offers what the phone does not — the full document, the approval history, and the manager's "All Approval Requests" view for tracking down stuck requests and reassigning approvers; see Approvals .

Path: /mobile/mfg/fpi.html | First-piece verification after setup and before production
Lists the dispatches awaiting first-piece inspection. A dispatch may only start once FPI passes; a failure means re-adjusting the machine and inspecting again. Only dispatches whose operation is set to require FPI appear here — an empty list usually means there are none right now, not that the screen is broken.
First article screen (two dispatches awaiting FPI, badged "Pending FPI")

1
Narrow the list by typing a work order or machine in the search bar (optional).
2
Tap "Start FPI" on the dispatch to open the FPI measurement screen.
3
On the measurement screen choose the verification level (VL), enter the measured values and the defect count, check the verdict and submit.
The fields and the way the measurement screen works are the same as for in-process inspection (IPQC); see that page.

First-piece inspection uses MIL-STD-1916 with Ac=0: any single defect fails it.
Result | What happens next
Pass | The dispatch is released to "Ready" and work can start. The message reads that FPI passed and work may begin.
Fail | The dispatch goes on hold (reason: first-piece inspection failed), and the message reads that FPI failed and the machine needs re-adjusting. After re-adjusting, QC resumes it on the desktop under Dispatch Operations → Handle hold, and the dispatch returns to "Pending FPI" to be inspected again.
Both a failed first-piece inspection and a failed in-process inspection (IPQC) put the dispatch on hold. The difference is where it goes when resumed: after a failed first piece it returns to "Pending FPI" to be measured again; after a failed IPQC it returns to "In Progress". A hold for a quality reason can only be resumed by someone with update permission on inspection orders.
