If the code is wrong or has expired, an error message appears and the screen stays on the verification step; tap "Back to username and password" to start again.
Mobile login screen (illustrative)
Enabling and registering 2FA on mobile uses the same setting as the desktop (My Settings > Two-factor authentication), so there is nothing extra to set up on the phone; once it is enabled on any device, logging in from any device needs the code.
Logout
Tap "Log out" at the top right.
Every header button carries a label under its icon (Back, Home, Log out and so on), and the buttons beside search fields are labelled "Scan", "Search", "Refresh", "Clear" and the like (from 2026-10-19).

After logging in, the home page shows the modules the account has access to as a grid; the usual ones are:
The home page (which modules appear depends on the account's permissions)
Shop floor (MFG)
Dispatch staging, starting/reporting/finishing, schedule enquiry, machine status, IPQC in-process inspection and first-piece inspection (FPI).
Inventory operations (INV)
Receipt put-away, issue and shipment picking, stock counting, stock balance enquiry and IQC incoming inspection.
My Approvals
Seeing the documents waiting for you and approving or rejecting them there and then; the number on the tile is how many are waiting. This one needs no mobile module permission and is the same list as the desktop's pending approvals — see My Approvals (Mobile) .
Which modules actually appear depends on the account's role permissions; with no mobile module permission at all, the home page shows "no mobile module permissions have been set" — ask your system administrator.
Shortcuts for production and reporting tasks
Inside "Production and reporting", the "Tasks" area at the top of the screen lists the tasks you can go straight to as icon-and-text buttons: Production Schedule 、 First-piece inspection 、 In-process inspection 、 Machine Status ; the "Production schedule" page also has Schedule Query and Preparation Board two buttons.
The shortcuts follow the role's mobile permissions: a role without "inspection (FPI/IPQC)", "machine status change" or "view production schedule" does not see the matching button, and the whole area is hidden when none is granted. Permissions are set under Mobile permission maintenance screen.
"Start / end work" and "Report" are not on the shortcut bar — they have to be done against a particular dispatch, so tap the dispatch card you want in the list below.
Staging
Tap a dispatch card and the "Staging" area lists this dispatch's Material not yet ready and the status of any staging order already raised; tapping "Create staging order" raises a draft (the staging warehouse comes from the work center default). Confirming the stock lock and actually picking and moving it are done on the desktop under Material Staging screen.
tooling does not have to be reported here — the tooling assigned during scheduling is used, and shot counting and tooling conflict detection are unaffected. Machine setup (tooling or line changeover) is timed separately with "Start setup" and "Setup done"; operations with no setup time defined show "no machine setup" and can start straight away.
The difference between reporting and finishing
During production you can multiple production reports (for example once per transfer batch); after reporting, people stay online and keep producing ; at the end of the session tap " Finish and report ", where you can report the final quantity at the same time (leave it blank to just clock out); the system closes the session and settles the hours. If production is not finished you can start again for another round; the dispatch closes automatically when the cumulative good quantity reaches the dispatched quantity.
If the connection drops just as you submit a report or completion, it is saved on the phone and sent automatically when the connection returns, and resending never double counts. The time recorded is when you tapped submit, not when it arrived.

C.H: Mobile guide (PWA) › Switching plant and push notifications
C.T:
Switching plant
The home page shows your current plant at the top, and "Switch" on the right changes it. What is listed depends on your role: a role with assigned plants sees only those, marked "Your role can use these plants" ; a role with just one shows "Your role is assigned to this plant only" ; a role with no restriction can use every plant in the system.
The switch plant panel (the current plant is marked "Current"; the others are the plants this role may use)
You cannot switch while the phone still holds entries waiting to be sent. The screen says "N item(s) are still waiting to sync — finish syncing before switching plant": what is queued belongs to the plant you were in , and sending it after a switch would file it under the wrong one. Get back online and let them go through (or confirm / discard them in the waiting list), then switch.
After a successful switch the page reloads itself , which is expected: the dispatch and machine lists on screen were read before the switch, and reloading replaces them with the new plant's data. The reload needs a connection, so switching plant is an online-only action anyway.
Your computer and phone share one active plant. If you switch plant on the phone, saving a screen that was already open on the computer before the switch is blocked with a message saying the screen was opened under one plant but your active plant is now another — nothing is saved , so the document cannot land in the wrong plant. What you typed stays on screen, and you are asked whether to switch back to the original plant and save what you filled in — OK switches back to the plant the screen was opened under and saves; Cancel leaves it unsaved. To create it in the new plant instead, refresh and fill it in again (refreshing clears the panel). Right after a system update, submitting a page opened before the update may likewise say the screen is missing its plant; refreshing fixes it.
Switched plant on another device: when you bring the home page back from the background, or return to it from another page, it re-reads your current plant and role automatically — no manual refresh needed.
Plant shows "No longer available — choose again": an administrator removed your current plant from your role. The home page opens the switch plant panel by itself; pick an available plant to carry on. Other screens show "Your current plant is no longer available… Go back to Home and choose a plant again."
Switching role
Below the plant row is your current role . "Switch" lists every role on your account; tap one to switch — the same rules as switching role on the computer. If the new role does not include your current plant, you are moved to that role's default plant. The page reloads afterwards, and as with switching plant, you cannot switch while entries are still waiting to be sent.
If the role shows "No longer available — choose again", an administrator removed the role you were using; choose one of the remaining roles here.
The approval list is also limited to the current plant. If a document you expect is missing on the phone, check which plant you are in first.
Push notifications
"Push notifications" (the bell) at the top right of the home page subscribes to or cancels push. The browser asks for notification permission the first time, and without it you cannot subscribe (the screen says "Allow notifications before subscribing to push"). Once subscribed the bell fills in and a yellow-bell "Test push" button appears; pressing it should deliver a test notification to the phone straight away, confirming the push channel works. You do not need it day to day.
For security the system accepts only the browsers' official push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft). Each account can subscribe up to 10 devices (adjustable by an administrator); beyond that the screen says "The device subscription limit has been reached" — cancel the subscription on a device you no longer use first.
You get a push when a document reaches you for approval, and tapping it opens the mobile "My Approvals" list rather than taking you to a desktop screen.
Push needs browser support and a ready service worker; an unsupported browser is told so rather than failing silently.

Each mobile screen below has its own page with a screenshot, the steps and the things to watch for. Whether a screen appears at all depends on the role's mobile permissions.
Shop floor (MFG)
Production
The floor's entry point to MFG: the shortcut bar, the machine and status filters and the dispatch list.
Production session
Setup (raising a staging order, starting and finishing setup) and starting and ending work.
Production report
Reporting good and defective quantities, the defect reason and the container; and the difference between the two submit buttons.
Requisition / Return
Request material from the production session, or raise a return slip for what is left.
Production Schedule
The schedule board grouped by work center and machine, with the query criteria and its limit.
Preparation Board
Checking material and tooling before work starts: the day switch, the staging badges and the three risk markers.
First Article (FPI)
First-piece verification after setup and before work starts; only a pass releases the dispatch.
In-Process QC (IPQC)
Sampling inspection during production; MIL-STD-1916 Ac=0, and a failure puts the dispatch on hold.
Machine Status
Scanning to report breakdowns, maintenance and standby; which events each status allows and what they do to dispatches.
Warehouse (INV)
The warehouse operations home page opens with the pending inbound and outbound counts, and the cards below it lead to the screens that follow.
The warehouse operations home page (the number on each card is how many are waiting)
Putaway
Choose an inbound document, then give the target location and quantity; one line can go to several locations.
Pick
Choose an outbound document, then use the available stock to decide the source location and quantity.
Stock Count
Counting by sheet, free counting and recounting, and when to use each.
Stock Query
By product (where is this thing) or by location (what is in this place).
Incoming Inspection (IQC)
Sampling incoming supplier material: choosing the verification level and what happens after a rejection.
WO Material Issue/Return
Pick slips from locations that hold stock, or receive returned material into a location, posting in one step.
Material Staging
Confirm staging orders to reserve stock, then move material into the staging area.
Outsource Receiving
Receive processed goods against the outsourcing PO; put them away once confirmed.

The mobile app needs a connection; it is not an offline app. Dispatches, stock, inspection orders and other screen data are always read live from the server. When the server cannot be reached the screen says "Connection required" instead of showing old data, which may already be wrong (a dispatch rescheduled, someone else having entered it).
Disconnection protection covers one situation only: the connection drops at the moment you tap submit (a brief Wi-Fi outage on the floor, the server restarting). The following entries are then saved on the phone and sent automatically when the connection returns, with another automatic attempt every minute; each carries a unique identifier, so resending never double counts:
Production reports, finish-and-report, clocking out, machine status changes (sent first)
Put-away, picking, stock counts (first count / recount)
Work-order issue/return posting, staging, requisition / return requests
The same applies when the signal is very weak : if there is no response within 20 seconds of tapping submit, the screen stops spinning and shows "saved, will be sent when connected". If the server had in fact already received and processed it, the resend just gets the same result back and nothing is counted twice — so when you see "saved", do not tap submit again .
When many people on the same line report at once (at a shift change, for example), the system retries automatically, so "the data was changed by someone else" now rarely appears. If it still does, that entry was not saved — just tap submit again; it will not be counted twice.
The time recorded is when you tapped submit, not when it arrived. For example, if you clock out at 10:00 and the connection only comes back at 10:20, the clock-out is still recorded at 10:00, so hours and downtime are not stretched.
Entries saved for more than 30 minutes are no longer sent automatically and become "Needs confirmation": check them in the waiting list (floating button at the bottom left of the home page) and tap "Confirm & send" if they are still correct; if you have already entered them on the desktop, tap "Discard" so they are not duplicated. The server no longer accepts entries older than 24 hours — enter those on the desktop and discard them.
Actions that work only while connected (never saved for later): approvals, clocking in, first-piece inspection, in-process inspection, incoming inspection, outsource receiving .
Buttons in the waiting list: "Sync now" sends immediately; failed items can be retried with "Retry failed items" or one by one with "Retry"; "Clear sent" removes the ones that went through.
Never sent on someone else's behalf : each held item remembers who pressed Submit. If someone else signs in, those items are marked "sign in as the original user to sync it" and wait until that person signs in.
Sign-out check : signing out while held items are still unsent asks for confirmation first; the items stay on this phone and are sent the next time the original user signs in.

Q: After I enter my username and password it just goes back to the login screen, with no error message. Why?
A: Check whether two-factor authentication is enabled on the account — once it is, logging in is not complete until the verification step is done, and this is not a failure. Only if the screen keeps returning and shows an error message is the username or password actually wrong.
Q: I have a new phone and the code in my authenticator app is different, so I cannot log in. What now?
A: This means the authenticator you registered has been lost. Ask your system administrator to reset two-factor authentication for the account; you will then have to scan the QR code again to register.
Q: The mobile home page says "no mobile module permissions have been set". Why?
A: The account has not been given access to any mobile module. Ask your system administrator to enable it in the role permissions.
Q: Items in the waiting list keep showing as failed. What should I do?
A: Read the red message first. If the server rejected it (for example the dispatch is already closed, or the quantity exceeds the dispatch), retrying will not help — check on the desktop, enter it there, then tap "Discard". If it simply could not connect at the time, make sure the connection is back and tap "Retry failed items". If you cannot tell, take a screenshot of the error message and send it to your system administrator.
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/mfg/ipqc.html | Sampling inspection while production is running
Lists the dispatches in progress for QC to sample during the process. It uses MIL-STD-1916 with Ac=0: any defect found puts the dispatch on hold.
In-process QC screen (the banner explains the Ac=0 rule)

1
Find the dispatch to inspect by typing a work order or machine in the search bar (optional).
2
Tap "Start IPQC" to open the measurement screen.
3
Choose the "VL" and the screen works out "Sample n" , "Accept Ac" and "Reject Re" from the lot size.
4
Enter each measured value under "Measurement Items" (the specification limits are shown); anything not listed can be added with "Add Item" .
5
Under "Ac=0 Batch Count" fill in the "Actual Sample" and the "NG Qty" ; the verdict updates immediately below.
6
Add remarks (what the defect was, what was done about it) and tap "Submit IPQC" .
The actual sample quantity has to be greater than zero or submitting warns that it must be. The screen shows the recommended sample size (at least n).

Result | What happens next
Pass | The dispatch stays in progress and production continues. The message reads that IPQC passed.
Fail | The whole lot is rejected, the dispatch is put on hold automatically and the screen tells you to notify QC. While on hold the floor cannot report, and QC has to clear it first.
Ac=0 means the acceptance number is zero: one defect in the sample rejects the whole lot. There is no acceptable percentage.
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/inv/iqc.html | Sampling inspection of incoming supplier material
Lists the receipts awaiting IQC. When a goods receipt is confirmed on the desktop, products that need inspecting raise an inspection order and appear here; the lot reaches the put-away list only once it passes. It also uses MIL-STD-1916 with Ac=0, so any defect rejects the whole lot.
Incoming inspection screen (a receipt selected, showing the sample size and the verdict)
Purchase receipts are listed once confirmed, and also after they have been put away into quarantine but not yet inspected; on acceptance they move to the warehouse on the receipt, or the item category's default when there is none, and acceptance is refused if neither is set. Besides ordinary purchase receipts, the list also shows goods returned on outsource receipts (marked "Outsource"). When they pass they are moved to a normal warehouse automatically (the warehouse on the receipt, otherwise the product category default) and added to the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity; failed quantities stay in quarantine awaiting disposition. If there is neither, a pass is refused with an explanation and the inspection is not recorded — set a default warehouse under Product Categories and inspect again.

1
Find the receipt with the search bar and tap it; "Back" switches to another one.
2
Check the "Received" and the product carried over.
3
Choose the "Verification Level (VL)" and the screen works out the "Required Sample n" from the received quantity; "Accept Ac" is always 0 and "Reject Re" always 1.
4
Enter the "Actual Sample Qty" (ideally not less than the required sample) and the "NG Qty (any NG = reject lot)" .
5
Check the "Result" , add remarks and tap "Submit IQC Result" .
The actual sample quantity has to be greater than zero, otherwise it warns that it must be.

C.H: Incoming Inspection (IQC) › Choosing the verification level
C.T:
The verification level decides how many pieces you sample: the higher the level the larger the sample, for the more critical parts.
Level | Use for
VL-I | The least strict, with the smallest sample.
VL-IV | The recommended default for ordinary IQC; use this unless told otherwise.
VL-VI | Critical components.
VL-VII | Safety-critical parts, with the strictest sampling.
VL-II, VL-III and VL-V are also available, with strictness between those above.

Result | What happens next
Pass | The lot is released and appears in the put-away list, ready to go into the good-stock warehouse.
Fail | The whole lot is rejected and never reaches the put-away list. What happens to it next — return, concession or rework — is decided by QA on the NCR screen on the desktop.
With Ac=0 there is no acceptable defect rate: one defect in the sample rejects the whole lot. If you are unsure about a lot, the right response is to raise the verification level and sample more, not to loosen the verdict.
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/inv/issue.html | The warehouse picks against material slips, or receives returned material into a location, and posts in one step
Opened from "WO Material Issue/Return" on the warehouse home page. Switch between "Issue" and "Return" at the top. The issue list holds in-plant issues, approved requisitions, outsource issues and rework issues; the return list holds return slips raised on the shop floor.
The "Work-Order Issue / Return" card on the warehouse home page shows how many slips are waiting (Issue N · Return M), matching the list inside.

1
Tap a slip. Each line shows the requested quantity and the locations that currently hold the product (warehouse / location, lot, on-hand quantity). If the work order has been staged, the staging location is marked "Staged" and listed first.
2
Tap the location you are picking from (for staged items the staging location is preselected, with a reminder to take it from there first) and change the "Issued" quantity if needed. If the staging location does not hold enough for the line, it is split into two entries automatically: the available quantity from the staging location and the shortfall from the next location that has stock. You can also tap "Add another location" to add an entry yourself, or ✕ to remove one. To take a whole box , scan its number into "Whole box: scan box number" ; the box's location and lot are filled in, and the quantity is what the box holds (no more than the line still needs).
3
Tap "Confirm issue & post" : picking and posting happen together; stock is deducted, the work order's issued quantity goes up and its reservation is consumed.
Lines with an issued quantity of 0 are not posted (not picked this time). A slip with no quantities cannot be submitted.
Staged material must be taken from the staging location first : whatever is still in the staging area for this work order has to be issued or requisitioned from the staging location; only the shortfall may come from other locations. This is checked when a desktop slip is saved, when the mobile slip is submitted and when it is posted; a violation is blocked with a message saying which location to use and how much. Returns are not affected.

1
Tap a return slip, scan or type the location it goes back into on each line, and check the "Received" quantity.
2
Tap "Confirm receipt & post" : the material comes back in at its original issue cost and the work order's returned quantity goes up.

C.H: WO Material Issue/Return › When the connection drops
C.T:
Pending slips need a connection to load. If the connection drops just as you post, the entry is saved on the phone and posted automatically once it returns. Stock and slip status are checked when it arrives; failures stay in the waiting list on the home page, and entries saved for more than 30 minutes become "Needs confirmation". See Disconnection protection .
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/mfg/machine-status.html | Reporting breakdowns, maintenance and standby from the floor
Scan the machine QR code or type the machine code, and the screen shows the machine's current status and the events available right now. What is available depends on the current status: only an available machine offers "Breakdown", and a retired machine offers nothing at all.
Machine status screen (the events available while the machine is Available)

1
Tap the scan button to scan the machine QR code with the camera, or type the code in the "Machine Code" field and look it up.
2
Check that the "Machine Name" and "Current Status" shown are the right ones.
3
Tap the event you want and the confirmation area opens below.
4
Add a "Note" if you want and tap "Confirm" .

The events available in each status are listed below. The two letters are the system code, shown at the right of each button:
Current status | Available events
Available | Breakdown DI, Start Maintenance HI, Set to Standby II, Enter Modification EO, Loan Out FO, Send for External Repair CO, Retire / Scrap GO
Standby | Restore to Available CI, Breakdown DI, Start Maintenance HI
Breakdown | Breakdown Resolved DO, Start Maintenance HI, Send for External Repair CO, Retire / Scrap GO
Maintenance | Maintenance Done HO, Breakdown DI, Retire / Scrap GO
External Repair | Restore to Available CI, Retire / Scrap GO
Modification | Restore to Available CI, Retire / Scrap GO
Loaned | Return from Loan FI
Retired | None — a retired machine offers no events.
These statuses and events use exactly the same wording as the desktop (which uses the same terms on the machine status order screen), so the floor and the office are talking about the same thing.

C.H: Machine Status › A status change affects dispatches
C.T:
When a machine moves to a status where it cannot run (breakdown or maintenance, for example), the system also deals with the dispatches on it and shows a dialog afterwards saying what was affected. When the machine goes back to available or standby, the dispatches held because it was down resume automatically:
Dispatch status | What the system does
Scheduled | Sent back to pending so it can be rescheduled onto another machine or slot.
Setup, Ready, Pending FPI, In Progress | Put on hold (reason: machine down), so the floor cannot carry on, and rescheduling does not move them. They return to their previous status automatically when the machine is back; for urgent work, production planning can switch them to another machine on the desktop under Dispatch Operations → Handle hold.
Check the machine code before submitting. A status change affects the schedule immediately, so scanning the wrong machine sends another line's dispatches back to pending.

C.H: Machine Status › When the connection drops
C.T:
If the connection drops just as you submit a status change, it is saved on the phone as the highest priority item and sent first when the connection returns — the sooner a stoppage reaches the system, the better the rescheduling. The stoppage is recorded at the moment you tapped submit , not when the connection came back. See Disconnection protection .
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/inv/outsource-receive.html | Receiving goods returned by a subcontractor against the outsourcing PO
Opened from "Outsource Receiving" on the warehouse home page. This step comes before "Putaway" : receive first, and the receipt appears in the put-away list once confirmed.
The "Outsource Receiving" card on the warehouse home page shows the number of open items: outsource purchase orders with quantity still to receive, plus approved receipts awaiting confirmation.
1
Type or scan the outsourcing PO number, or pick it from the list (only confirmed POs with an open quantity are shown).
2
Each line shows ordered, received, in-draft and open quantities. Enter the "Qty received" and lot; in simplified mode also give the location. Exceeding the open quantity asks for confirmation (the supplier may have over-delivered); whether it can be received follows the plant parameters "Outsource over-receipt tolerance" and "Outsource: beyond the tolerance" — by default only a supervisor with the over-quantity approval right can receive beyond the tolerance (see Plants ).
2a
When the plant has "Inspect outsource deliveries at receipt" on, also enter "Defects" on each line (defects found while sampling; 0 if none); the location is optional and defaults to the product category. Defects cannot exceed the quantity received.
3
Tick "Final delivery" when the supplier has delivered everything, then tap "Confirm receipt" .
Returned goods are inspected first: after confirming, products that are not inspection-exempt can only be put away into quarantine under "Putaway", then inspected under "Incoming Inspection" (marked "Outsource" in the list); once they pass, the system moves them to a normal warehouse, and only then is the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity updated. That warehouse is the product category's default warehouse/location (the phone does not ask for one); if a product that needs inspection has no category default, submitting is blocked with the product named — set it under Product Categories first.
With inspection at receipt there is no putaway and no separate incoming inspection: 0 defects = pass, stocked into a normal warehouse and added to the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity; any defect (Ac=0) = the whole lot goes to quarantine for nonconformance handling. If "Issue send-out materials at receipt" is also on, the send-out materials for a rejected lot are still deducted (the vendor has used them); their cost goes into quarantine with the lot, and the later disposition (rework, return to vendor, scrap) decides where it ends up.
Outsourced-operation orders (the screen shows an "Outsourced operation" note) need no location: what comes back is work in progress and is not stocked; submitting adds it to that operation's dispatch completed quantity and deducts the operation's input materials at the same time.

The processing price, currency and exchange rate always come from the outsourcing PO and the rate table; no amounts are entered on the phone. Depending on settings there are three outcomes:
Confirmed, awaiting put-away : put it into a location under "Putaway".
Confirmed and stocked (simplified mode, or inspection at receipt): stock is already posted; lots that failed at-receipt inspection are in quarantine.
Sent for approval : when receiving has an approval workflow, the receipt appears under "Approved receipts awaiting confirmation" at the top of this page once approved; tap "Confirm" to finish.
Confirming a receipt also creates the AP invoice, so it can only be submitted online ; tapping twice does not create two receipts.
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/inv/pick.html | Taking stock from a location against an outbound document
The mirror image of put-away, in two steps: pick an outbound document, then give the source location and the quantity. The documents are likewise raised on the desktop (material issues, shipments, scrap, loans, sample shipments, purchase returns and so on).
Pick screen (step 1: choosing an outbound document)

The list shows every outbound document line with its number, product and required quantity, and a type badge saying whether it is an issue, a shipment or something else. Narrow it with the search bar.

1
Check the "Doc No." , "Product" and "Required" quantity.
2
The "Stock by Location" section lists where this product is held and how much is at each location, so you can decide where to pick from.
3
Scan or type the code in "Source Location" and enter the "Pick Qty" . Tapping a row under Stock by Location fills in the location too (and the lot, for rows that have one). To pick a whole box, scan the box QR: the box's location and lot are filled in, and the quantity is the smaller of the box contents and the quantity required.
4
Tap "Confirm Pick" ; on success it shows "Pick successful" .
If Stock by Location says "No stock records" , the product has no stock in any location. Check whether it needs to be received or transferred first rather than forcing a location through.
One line can be picked from several locations in turn; the required quantity counts down each time.

As with put-away: the list needs a connection to load, and if the connection drops just as you submit, the entry is saved on the phone and sent automatically when it returns. See Disconnection protection .

Path: /mobile/mfg/preparation.html | Checking material and tooling before work starts
Organised around the day production is planned, this board lists what each work center is due to run and whether the material is ready, for the pre-shift check. It is read-only.
Preparation board (it opens on tomorrow; each card carries a staging status badge)

The three buttons at the top switch the day, and "Tomorrow" is the default — the board exists so that material for tomorrow is ready today, which is why it does not open on today. Tap "Custom" to pick any date.

C.H: Preparation Board › What is on a card
C.T:
Dispatches are grouped by work center. Each card shows the dispatch number, the product name, the quantity, the setup time in minutes and the planned start and finish, plus a staging status badge:
Badge | Guide
Staged | The material is ready and work can start.
Staging | A staging order exists and the warehouse is still picking and moving the material.
Not Staged | No staging order has been raised yet; deal with it promptly or the start will slip.
The three colours in the legend mark dispatches that need attention: "Tooling Conflict" means the same tool is scheduled for overlapping slots, "Material Risk" means the material may not arrive in time, and "Predicted Late" means it is projected to miss the planned finish time. Dispatches marked "Continued" started on an earlier day and are still running, so they need no preparation.
When you see "Not Staged" or "Material Risk", open that dispatch's production session screen and raise a staging order; the warehouse then locks and picks the stock on the desktop.
SmartFactory MES User Manual | Contact your system administrator if you need help

Path: /mobile/mfg/reports.html | Reporting good and defective quantities
Opened from the production session screen by tapping "Report". You have to have started work first — opening this page directly shows "no session ID, please start work first" and nothing can be submitted.
Production report screen (the progress card shows reported, remaining and total)

1
Enter the "Good Qty" and "NG Qty" . At least one of them has to be greater than zero, otherwise submitting warns that one of the two must be filled in.
2
When the defective quantity is greater than zero the "NG Reason" dropdown appears; choose the matching reason.
3
The "Container (optional)" field is optional. Tap the dashed box to open the camera and scan a barcode, or tap the text below it to type one instead. You can also scan a box number, and the good quantity is recorded on that box; if the box cannot be used (for example it already holds some other work order's work in process), the report still goes through but the box is not linked, and the success message explains why.
4
Choose how to submit (see below); once sent, the entry is listed under "This session's reports" at the bottom of the page.

C.H: Production report › The difference between the two submit buttons
C.T:
Button | What it does
Submit Report (keep producing) | Reports this batch's quantity and keeps the session open, so the operator stays on the job. It can be used as often as needed during production — once per container, for example.
Finish and Report (end this session) | Reports the final quantity and ends the session, settling the hours at the same time. It asks for confirmation first.
If production is not finished, you can return to the production session screen and start another round after ending a session; the dispatch closes automatically once the cumulative good quantity reaches the dispatched quantity.
The cumulative good quantity cannot exceed the dispatch quantity unless the plant sets an "In-plant over-production tolerance" (at 3%, a dispatch of 100 can be reported up to 103). Beyond that it is rejected by default; if the plant requires supervisor confirmation, only a supervisor with the over-quantity approval right can report it. Route: /DeliveryRate | On-time shipment statistics per order
Measures the on-time shipment rate of sales orders, grouped by customer.
The population is what was due to ship in the period, not what actually shipped in it: the date range is matched against the promised date , and each order line is counted exactly once, with three possible outcomes:
Fully shipped — the date the last shipment completed the line is compared with the promised date; shipping on the day itself counts as on time. With split shipments it is the last batch that matters, not the first.
Past the promised date and still not complete — counted as late .
Not yet due — excluded.
The basis changed on 2026-09-21 and most historical figures fall: The old population contained only goods already shipped , so an order past its promised date but not yet shipped was absent from the denominator — the very lines the Overdue Sales Orders report lists were invisible here. The new basis counts them. Two other things are fixed at the same time: orphan shipment lines that match no order line no longer enter the denominator (they used to make on-time plus late fail to add up to the total), and a line promised inside the period but shipped after it used to fall through both periods and disappear; it now appears in the period its promised date belongs to.
Delivery rate screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Guide

Late | Number of lines completed after the promised date, or past the promised date and still not shipped in full
Attainment % | On-time lines ÷ due lines, i.e. delivery performance for that customer

Status | Guide

Shipment
1
Click "Add" and pick the sales order to bring in the open lines and the available stock.

Enter the quantity shipped and the shipping warehouse/location, then save and submit or confirm.

Before voiding a shipment, void its AR invoice (reverse any receipts first) and any sales returns that reference it; voiding only reverses inventory and cost, never the invoice or the returns. In full warehouse mode the AR invoice is issued as soon as the shipment is confirmed, so void it before cancelling the confirmation; confirming again issues a new invoice from the latest content.

The full outsourcing cycle: quotation → outsource PO → material issue → receipt → rework / reconciliation
The OSP (Outsourcing) module manages subcontracted operations in one place: the outsource quotation master holds the price per subcontractor and operation, outsource purchase orders are raised by MRP or by hand, outsource material documents send raw material to the subcontractor, and finished parts come back through an outsource receipt where the actual material usage determines the Scrap Penalty , while processing rejects are tracked for cost and claim allocation on an outsource rework document. Confirming a receipt creates the outsource AP invoice (FIN) automatically, and outsource progress plus the outsource reconciliation report (RPT) show the material at the subcontractor and reconcile the charges.

The unit cost of an outsource issue is frozen at the moment of issue (AVCO), which is what the scrap penalty is priced at, so later changes in stock cost do not affect material already issued. C.H: Outsource Price Analysis › How it is calculated
C.T:
The monthly trend is converted to local currency and weighted by quantity
Average prices in the chart and the monthly table are in local currency (unit price × the exchange rate on that receipt), so subcontractors quoting in different currencies can be read on one chart. Averaging transaction-currency prices directly would add USD 30 to TWD 30 and halve it — a meaningless number that looks perfectly normal.
The average is weighted by receipt quantity : without weighting, a one-piece trial run would count as much as a 10,000-piece production run, and the trend would follow the small odd orders.
"Not comparable" is not "zero difference"
The difference column shows "—" rather than 0, for two quite different reasons. The yellow badge above the table tells you how many lines are affected:
No quotation found — this subcontractor has never quoted this product, and there is no supplier-level catch-all quotation either. This is a gap in quotation maintenance ; the quotation master needs updating.
Currency mismatch — for example the quotation is in USD and the receipt in TWD. That is a conversion issue, not a price variance.
It compares against the quotation of the day, not today's
Every receipt is compared against the quotation in effect on its own receipt date . For a product whose price changed mid-period, the receipts taken at the old price are therefore not all counted as variances. The lookup order is identical to the one used when the outsource PO was created (supplier + product + routing + operation, falling back from the most specific), so the "what it should have been" in this report is the same answer the system used at the time.

Route: /SupplierDeliveryRate | On-time delivery statistics per supplier
Measures the on-time delivery rate (OTD rate) of purchases and outsourcing, with a monthly trend line and a supplier delay ranking, as input to supplier evaluation.
The population is what was due in the period, not what was received in it: the date range is matched against the promised date , and each purchase order line (or, for outsourcing, each outsource PO) is counted exactly once, with three possible outcomes:
Fully received — the date the last receipt completed the line is compared with the promised date. Not the first receipt: a line whose first batch arrived on time but whose last batch took three months counts as late.
Past the promised date and still not complete — counted as late , with the overdue days measured against today, so they keep growing while the delay continues.
Not yet due — excluded. There is no outcome yet, and including these would make the rate drift with however many future orders happen to be open.
The basis changed on 2026-09-21, so historical figures are lower than before: The old basis looked only at goods already received , so an order that was simply never delivered never entered the denominator — the longer a supplier stalled, the cleaner the denominator and the better the rate looked. One supplier showed two overdue lines on the Overdue Purchase Orders report while this report showed 100%. The new basis counts those lines, so a lower number is a correction , not a decline. The delivery dimension of supplier evaluation shares this basis and falls with it.

Route: /VendorEvaluation | Annual and quarterly evaluation of qualified suppliers (SRM)
Evaluates suppliers annually or quarterly: quality and delivery scores are calculated by the system, price and service scores are entered manually, and the total is a weighted average. Approving an evaluation updates the supplier qualification status on the company master (Qualified / Under Watch / Suspended), which then warns buyers on purchase and outsource orders.
Vendor evaluation screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Quality Score = (1 − NCR reject quantity ÷ posted receipt quantity) × 100. The reject quantity is the sum of QCR non-conformance reports (source = goods receipt, not voided) within the period, summed across all plants. With no receipts at all in the period the score cannot be computed : the screen shows "No data for period" and the dimension is excluded from the weighting rather than scored 100.
2
Delivery Score = on-time delivery rate × 100, on the same basis as the "Supplier Delivery Rate" report (both purchase and outsource, with the population being lines whose promised date falls in the period). With nothing due in the period the score again cannot be computed : it shows "No data for period" and is excluded from the weighting.
3
Score weights Stored in the system parameters srm_weight_quality / delivery / price / service (30/30/20/20 by default) and adjustable by the administrator.
"No data" is not the same as "full marks": A supplier you have never traded with and a supplier with zero defects and perfect delivery used to receive exactly the same score , although only the latter had earned it. A dimension that cannot be computed now drops out of the weighting, and its weight is redistributed across the rest ; when none of the four can be computed the total is 0 rather than a division by zero. The list, the form and the printout all mark it "No data for period" — the printout goes to people outside the company, so a placeholder score must not be allowed to read as an assessment there.

1
Click "New Evaluation", pick the supplier and year (leave the quarter blank for an annual evaluation), click "Recalculate" to pull in the automatic scores and their basis, then enter the price and service scores; the total is calculated as you type.
2
Total ≥ 80 Qualified, 60–79 Conditional, < 60 Failed; A follow-up action is mandatory when the result is Failed . A supplier can have only one evaluation per period.
3
Once submitted, the draft follows the approval template (no template = approved immediately). Approval writes the qualification status back automatically: Qualified → Qualified, Conditional → Probation, Failed → Suspended (with a red warning when ordering).

The QCR (Quality Control) module manages the three inspection stages and closes the loop on nonconforming material: IQC incoming inspection (triggered by a goods receipt or an outsource receipt, with MIL-STD-1916 sampling, VL switching and skip-lot), IPQC in-process inspection (triggered by an operation flag) and FQC final inspection (a hard gate on completion receipt). Route: /InspectionOrder | Managing and judging IQC/IPQC/FQC inspection orders
Inspection orders are triggered by a goods or outsource receipt (IQC), by reporting an operation (IPQC) or by completion (FQC). The sample size is calculated automatically to MIL-STD-1916 (Ac=0), with verification level (VL) switching and skip-lot after consecutive acceptances. The inspector enters the measured values or the judgement and then either accepts the lot or raises an NCR. Inspections can also be carried out on a mobile device.
Inspection order enquiry screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

1
Enter your criteria on the query bar and click "Search"; column headers can be clicked to sort, and the paging controls sit below the list.
2
Can be filtered by inspection stage, status, item and source document number.

IQC incoming inspection (desktop entry)
1
Click "IQC pending entry" at the top right to open the pending list, which is exactly the same as IQC pending on mobile (with VL switching and skip-lot already applied).
2
Select a receipt line and click "Enter"; the panel fills in the lot size and the suggested sample size, and the verification level (VL-1 to VL-7) can be changed.
3
Enter the actual sample size and the number of defects and submit. With Ac=0, one defect or more rejects the whole lot.
4
On acceptance the system transfers the stock out of the quarantine warehouse into the warehouse and location named on the receipt line (or the item category's default when the line has none). This is a system transfer that posts directly without approval, and the payable is accrued for the released quantity at the same time. If neither is set, the acceptance is refused with an explanation and nothing is recorded. On rejection the stock stays in quarantine and is handled through an NCR. The pending list covers receipts confirmed and awaiting put-away as well as receipts already put away into quarantine but not yet inspected.
FPI first-piece inspection (desktop entry)
1
Click "FPI pending entry" at the top right to open the list of dispatches awaiting a first piece. It lists every dispatch whose operation requires a first-piece inspection and has not passed FPI yet — whether or not staging has been done.
2
Select a dispatch and click "Enter"; the panel fills in the dispatched quantity and the suggested sample size, and the verification level (VL-1 to VL-7) can be changed.
3
Enter the actual sample size and the number of defects and submit. With Ac=0, one defect or more is a fail.
4
Pass → the dispatch is unlocked to "staging done" and work can start; fail → the dispatch goes on hold (reason: first-piece inspection failed), and dispatches on hold do not appear in the pending FPI list. Once the problem is sorted out, resume it under Dispatch Operations → Handle hold ; the dispatch returns to "Pending FPI" and the first piece is entered again.
First-piece inspection gate: If the operation has "first-piece inspection required" ticked, then until FPI passes work can never start — on the desktop or on mobile, and whether or not staging was done. What counts is whether the dispatch already has a passing first-piece inspection, not the dispatch's current status, so starting work directly without staging is still blocked. The first piece can be entered from either the desktop or a mobile device.
Entering pending IPQC / FQC / RQC inspections
1
Query inspection orders with the status "pending" and click a line to open the panel.
2
Enter the actual sample size, the number of defects and any notes at the bottom of the panel and submit the result.
3
When IPQC fails, the system automatically puts the related running dispatch on hold (reason: in-process inspection failed). After QC has confirmed, resume it under Dispatch Operations → Handle hold ; a hold for a quality reason needs update permission on inspection orders to be resumed.
Carrying out an inspection (mobile)
1
Open a pending inspection order; the system has already filled in the inspection items and the sample size from the spec.
2
Enter the measured value or judgement for each item; anything out of spec is flagged automatically.
3
All pass → judged accepted and closed (the IQC accepted quantity goes into stock, FQC releases the receipt).
4
Fail → an NCR is raised and goes into the disposition process.
The IQC queue also includes outsource receipts (marked "Outsource" next to the number): like ordinary receipts, returned goods can only be put into quarantine until they pass, are then released to a normal warehouse automatically, and update the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity.
Printing
The button on each row of the list (print permission required) opens a printout with a QR code in a new tab, ready to print or save as PDF. The inspection printout shows the source document, product name, lot size and sample size, and for each item the spec limits, target, measured value and result, so it can serve as the shop-floor measurement record.

C.H: Data Audit Diagnostics › Cumulative fields that can be corrected automatically
C.T:
One kind of difference has a known correct answer without any investigation: progress fields on documents whose value is fully determined by the source documents. There are two today — PO line received quantity (should be the total received on all non-void goods receipts) and SO line shipped quantity (should be the total shipped on all non-void shipments). When such differences exist, an amber card at the top of the screen lists each one with its current value, the value it should be and the difference.
1
Tick the rows to correct (or select all), click "Correct selected" and confirm. You need change permission on Data Audit.
2
On submit the system recalculates the correct value instead of writing the number shown on screen — anything received or shipped between viewing the screen and clicking submit is included. Only documents of your current plant are changed.
3
The before and after values of every correction and who made it are recorded in the Audit Log (entity type PurchaseOrderLine / SalesOrderLine, entity ID "number|line").
Differences in journals, inventory quantities and cost are never corrected automatically: their cause has to be found first, and simply making the numbers agree would wipe out the evidence. Goods receipts pointing at a PO line that does not exist (orphans) cannot be corrected automatically either and stay in the findings below.

C.H: Data Audit Diagnostics › Inventory GL vs subledger
C.T:
The other inventory checks compare quantities ; this group compares amounts . The inventory GL account (1401) must equal the value of the inventory subledger (FIFO cost layers plus on-hand quantity × average cost for moving-average items). After removing the three adjustments below, which by design never reach the general ledger, the residual must be 0.
Work in progress : production and outsourcing issues post no journal, so issued material stays in the inventory account until the finished goods are received back into stock. It is worked out per work order (issues, returns, completions, outsource receipts and the completion absorption entry).
Customer-supplied material (CI/CR): owned by the customer, so only the quantity is tracked.
Lent out (IL/LR): ownership does not change, only the location does.
Audit type | Meaning and what to do
Inventory GL ≠ subledger | A residual remains after the adjustments: some movement was posted without a journal, or with a different amount. Blocks the month-end close. Use the "Document GL ≠ movement value" findings for the same plant to find the documents; once the cause is known, correct it with a manual journal — the finding clears when the residual is 0.
Document GL ≠ movement value | Listed only while there is a residual, to show where it comes from: this document's inventory GL amount differs from the value of its stock movements and is not one of the adjustments above. Does not block the close on its own (the residual does).
Negative work-order WIP | More value came back to stock than was issued — for example a return larger than what was actually issued in-plant, or an outsource receipt whose processing fee was never posted. Blocks the close.
WIP left on closed work order | The work order is closed or voided, yet the issued material was neither costed into the finished goods nor returned to stock. Blocks the close.
Stock movements recorded before journal posting existed have no journals and will keep showing up in the residual; correct such historical differences the same way, with one manual journal debiting or crediting the inventory account against a suitable adjustment account.

C.H: Data Audit Diagnostics › Points to note
C.T: The screen only shows exceptions for your current plant (plus those with no plant dimension), so 0 exceptions does not mean the whole company is clean. Audit results are kept for 90 days and then cleared automatically. Make sure this screen is clear before the month-end close, or the same checks will block it.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Audit Type | The consistency check to run; leave blank to scan every check in one pass
Result fields
Field | Guide
Audit Type | Name of the audit check that found the problem
Document / Key | The document number or summary key where the problem is, for locating the data
Item | Item involved (applies to some audit checks)
Plant | Plant the problem belongs to
Difference | The amount or quantity by which the two bases disagree; 0 means they agree
Guide | Description of the difference and the suggested way to handle it
The audit itself only detects and reports differences; apart from the "cumulative fields" above, corrected only when someone ticks and approves them, it never changes data. Anything within the tolerance is left out of the results.
Month-end close 、 Accounting period

Route: /FieldTelemetry | What happens on the phones that the server cannot see: page errors, slow or unreachable APIs, disconnections, unsent data
When the floor reports "the phone is slow", "nothing happens when I tap" or "my report disappeared", the server's records only show the half where the request arrived . A script error on the page, a request that never got through, a signal so weak that every API takes over ten seconds, entries stuck unsent on a phone — all of that happens on the phone. Every phone reports these once a minute, and this screen brings them together.

1
Pick the period at the top right: the last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days.
2
Four KPI cards: the number of page errors ; the share of API calls over 3 seconds (with the number that were unreachable or failed underneath; turns amber above 5%); the number of disconnections and their total minutes; and the number of phones with unsent data (amber if there are any).
3
Phones : for each phone, when it last reported, who was using it, network type and latency, version, and how many entries are still unsent and how long the oldest has waited . Phones with unsent data are listed first with an amber background — the person using it may believe the work has already been reported.
4
Top page errors : for each error, the page, how often it happened, on how many phones and when it was last seen. An error that many phones hit is usually a software problem rather than a problem with one phone.
5
API response times and failures : for each API, the number of calls, average and longest time, how many took 3–10 seconds or over 10 seconds, how many were unreachable or failed, and how many conflicts there were (someone else changed the same document at the same moment and three automatic retries still conflicted; that entry was not saved and the phone sends it again). Conflicts concentrated on a few lines mean several people there often work on the same dispatch at once. Rows with failures or calls over 10 seconds are shown in red. Document numbers, machine codes and the like in the address are shown as {id} , so that calls to the same API add up.
6
Recent events : each error, disconnection and queue report one by one, filterable by kind; expand "Details" on an error to see the stack trace.

C.H: Field Telemetry › How to read it
C.T:
One line keeps saying it is slow : check network and latency for those phones under "Phones"; latency of several hundred milliseconds, or many calls over 3 seconds in the API table at the same time, usually points to the Wi-Fi in that area rather than the system.
Only one API is slow : if everything else is fine and only that one is slow, the query behind it on the server is the problem — pass it to system maintenance.
A phone has had unsent data for a long time : ask that user to open the waiting list on the phone's home page; anything older than 30 minutes stops at "awaiting confirmation" until they tap "Confirm and send" or "Discard" (see "Disconnection protection" in the mobile manual).

All times are when the server received the report (phone clocks are not trusted), so errors that happen while a phone is offline only appear after it reconnects. The screen shows your current plant plus reports with no plant (for example errors on the sign-in page, or after a session expired). No request content is collected; the phone code is a random value the phone's browser generates itself, not a hardware identifier, and it changes if the browser data is cleared. Data is kept for 30 days and then cleared automatically. By default only the Admin, HQ, manager and finance roles can see this screen.

Route: /ReportInbox | Download the scheduled reports addressed to you
Report files produced by schedules and addressed to you appear here. The system never emails reports as attachments — once an attachment is sent it is permanently outside access control, whereas a file kept here has its permission re-checked on every download.

C.H: Report Inbox › How to use it
C.T:
1
Set a run-date range (optional) and click Search.
2
Find the report you need and check the data range — a schedule stores a relative period such as "last month", which is converted into absolute dates at each run.
3
Click Download to get the file. It is named after the schedule and the run date.

The list only shows successful runs that produced a file; failed or skipped runs are on the Schedule Run History screen. If your permission for that report has been revoked you cannot download the file even while it still exists.

Route: /ReportSchedule | Produce routine reports automatically and deliver them to the inbox
Set a report to be produced automatically every day, week or month, and delivered to the Report Inbox of the people you nominate. The system sends no email — the report stays inside the system, and permission is re-checked when the recipient downloads it, so people who have left or changed jobs can no longer get the file.
Report schedules screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

C.H: Report Schedules › How to use it
C.T:
1
Click Add Schedule to open the side panel, give the schedule a name and pick the report to produce. The dropdown only lists reports you are currently authorized to run. Once a report is chosen, a Period field appears below it if that report needs one; pick a rolling period such as "Last month". Reports that need no period — stock valuation, for instance, which shows the position as it stands — do not show the field.
2
Choose the frequency: daily needs only a time; weekly also needs a day of the week; monthly also needs a day of the month.
3
Choose the output format (Excel or CSV) and the recipients. There can be several; the system produces one file per language used by the recipients, so English users do not receive a Chinese report.
4
Click Save. The screen shows the next run time, displayed and calculated in the plant time zone. To verify the setting immediately, click Run Now and the report will be produced within about a minute.

Schedules only run where the Report Tools feature is switched on; when it is off they do not run and the startup log states how many are affected. Runs missed during downtime are not caught up — re-running "last month" gives the same answer, but re-running "yesterday" would pick the wrong day, so nothing is caught up. At run time the owner's permission for the report is checked again; if it has been revoked the schedule is disabled automatically and the reason is recorded in the run history, never silently stopped. A report covers only the data of the schedule's plant: if a run succeeds with 0 rows, first check that the Plant column shows the plant where the data lives.

Query criteria
Condition | Guide
Schedule Name | Filters by keyword in the name
Report | Shows schedules for one report only
Plant | Lists only the current plant's schedules by default; choose All plants to see every plant's schedules
Active only | Hides disabled schedules when ticked
Setting fields
Field | Guide
Target plant | Read-only. When adding, it is the plant you are currently in; when editing, the plant the schedule was created for. The report covers this plant's data only, and the period and run time follow its time zone. To schedule for another plant, switch to that plant first
Schedule Name | Must be unique per person; it also forms part of the downloaded file name
Report | The report to produce; only those you may run are listed
Period | What is stored is a rolling period such as "Last month" or "Yesterday", resolved into actual dates on every run rather than a fixed date range. The field appears only for reports that need a period, and is compulsory when it does
Frequency | Daily, weekly or monthly — these three only
Day of Week | Applies to weekly schedules
Day of Month | Applies to monthly schedules; 29–31 falls back to the last day in shorter months
Hour / Minute | Time of day the schedule runs
Output Format | Excel keeps column formatting; CSV is easier to import elsewhere
Recipients | The report lands in their inbox; each download re-checks their permission
Enable this schedule | Disabled schedules no longer run automatically
Next Run | Calculated from the frequency and recalculated whenever the setting changes; shown in the time zone of the schedule's plant, with the zone printed below the time

Store a set of query criteria and re-run them with one click
When " My saved queries " and " Save this query " appear above a report's search bar, that report supports saved queries. They solve the chore of re-entering the same criteria every time: save once, then pick it from the dropdown to re-run with those criteria.

C.H: Saved Queries › How to use it
C.T:
1
Set the criteria on the report and run the search once, to confirm the result is what you want.
2
Click "Save this query", give it a name you will recognise (for example "Plant A overdue purchases last month"), and pick a period (see below).
3
From then on, pick it from the "My saved queries" dropdown to re-run. Remove ones you no longer need with the delete button in the dropdown.

C.H: Saved Queries › The period is stored as "last month", not as a fixed date range
C.T:
This is deliberate, and it is the one field you must fill in
Reports that take a period require a relative period when saved (today, last week, last month, this quarter…). A "last month's sales ranking" stored as fixed dates would still show that same month when opened next month — the opposite of what a saved query is for. With a relative period it is recalculated each time you open it.
Some reports offer fewer period options, deliberately
Accounting and financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss, trial balance) offer only "this accounting period / last accounting period". Accounting periods can have custom start and end dates that differ from calendar months, so "last month" — although it would run — would not be the period you had in mind at a plant using custom periods.
Annual reports (purchase amount analysis) offer only "this year / last year". That screen selects a year and shows twelve months, so "last month" would quietly widen into a whole year.

Item | Guide
Who can see them | Saved queries are personal : only you see yours; they are not shared with your department or role
How permission is checked | Permission is re-evaluated as you are now every time you open one. If your permissions change, an old saved query is blocked with a reason rather than running under the permissions it was saved with
Which criteria are stored | Only the fields visible on that report's search bar. Criteria the screen cannot express are not stored, and you are told which were dropped when you save
Plant | Not stored. A re-run always uses the plant you are currently switched to , so the same saved query returns that plant's data

C.H: Saved Queries › Which reports have it
C.T:
Twenty-two reports currently support saved queries, across inventory, sales, purchasing, outsourcing, manufacturing, accounting and financial statements. Telling them apart is straightforward: look for the two buttons above the search bar . If they are absent the report has not been included yet — it is not a permission problem.
A saved query comes first, then a schedule
To have a report produced automatically and sent to recipients, the flow is save it as a saved query first, then add a schedule under "Report Schedules" . There is deliberately no shortcut that turns the current search straight into a schedule: a schedule runs again and again, so it is worth confirming the criteria once first.

Menu: System Administration → Audit Log | Permission: per permission settings (read-only screen)
The audit log records data changes in the system: who did what, to which record, and when , together with the source IP address. This screen is read-only : entries are written automatically by the system and nobody can add, change or delete them here.
Audit log screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Criterion | Guide
Keyword | Matched against both the user name and the entity ID . To see the history of one document, paste its number here.
Entity Type | A drop-down listing the entity types that actually occur in the data (for example Mobile.Permission ). A type that has never occurred is not offered.
Action | Filters by the kind of change (create, update, delete and so on).
Start Date / End Date | Filters by the time of the change; the whole of both days is included (entries on the end date itself are covered). Days are counted in your own time zone , matching what the Timestamp column shows: a change made in the early hours belongs to that day and is not missed.
Include unplanted records | By default you see only entries for the plant you are currently in . Tick it to additionally include entries that belong to no plant: changes to company-wide settings such as users, roles and permissions fall into this group.
Cannot find a change to a user or a permission? Tick "Include unplanted records" first: settings like these belong to no plant, so the default plant filter hides them and the screen looks as though nobody ever touched them. From 21 October 2026, changes to records that have no plant of their own (document lines, users, roles, permissions, shared master data) are filed under the plant the person making the change was in , so they show by default; older entries still need the box ticked.

Field | Guide
Timestamp | When the change happened, converted to the time zone of your plant for display (internally it is stored in UTC). Sorted newest first by default.
User | The user name of whoever made the change. The name recorded here remains even if the account is later deleted.
Action | The kind of change: create, update, delete and so on.
Entity Type | The kind of record that was changed.
Entity ID | The identifier of the record changed; for documents it is usually the document number. A document line is recorded as "number|line" (for example RC-2610-00001|2): searching by the document number lists its lines too, and tells you which line was changed.
IP address | The source address the change came from.

Tracing what was changed on a document
1
Choose "System Administration > Audit Log" in the left-hand menu.
2
Paste the document number into the keyword box, narrow the date range if needed, and click "Search".
3
Click "Details" at the right of the row; the panel that opens shows the changes made — which fields, and from what value to what.
Seeing what one person did
1
Type their user name in the keyword box, set the date range and search.
2
Click the "Timestamp" or "Action" headings to change the sort order, which helps to spot bursts of activity in a particular period.

The current results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the timestamp, user, action, entity type, entity ID and IP address. The detailed changes are not part of the export ; those have to be opened one entry at a time.
The export applies the current criteria, including the date range and "Include unplanted records", so get the results you want on screen first . Audit data is usually voluminous, and an export with no date range can take a long time.
