C.H: Code Maintenance › What each category feeds (master data)
C.T:
The table below covers the categories used by the master-data screens. There are more categories than these : other modules bring their own, such as ng_reason for defect reasons, downtime_type for downtime types and PZ.SalesOrderType for order types. What the "Category" drop-down on screen lists is the authority.
Category | Which field on which screen it feeds
payment_type | Company / Vendor Master — payment type
abc_grade | Company / Vendor Master — customer grade
stock_mode | Product Master — stock mode
mrp_mode | Product Master — planning mode
tooling_type | Tooling Master — type
special_day_type | Special Day — day type
location_type | Warehouse (storage location) — location type
The category drop-down at the top of the screen lists the categories that actually exist in your data . So when you add the first code of a category, type the category into the "Category" box yourself; it appears in the drop-down from then on.

Adding a drop-down option
1
Choose "System Administration > Code Maintenance" in the left-hand menu, pick a category (or type a keyword) and click "Search".
2
Click "Add"; if a category was selected in the search, the form is pre-filled with it.
3
Fill in the code, the Chinese and English names and the sort order, then click "Save".
4
Back on the master-data screen the new option appears in the drop-down — or, if approval applies, once it has been approved.

If an administrator has switched on approval for the Document Approval Settings of "Code Maintenance", both adding and changing go through approval here:
What you do | What happens
Add | After saving the status is pending approval and the code is set to inactive ; it only takes effect and appears in the drop-down after approval.
Change | It has to be submitted again , and stays inactive while it is pending. Changing a code already in use therefore makes it disappear from the drop-down for a while.
A code under approval | Cannot be edited or deleted until the approval finishes or is withdrawn.
No approval configured | It takes effect on save, and you control "Active" yourself.
Approval settings are per plant: whether code maintenance needs approval depends on the setting for the plant you are currently in . The same code may need approval when handled in plant A but not in plant B; that follows from the settings and is not a fault.

The system checks whether the code is used by actual data — for example "in use by a company (payment type)", "in use by a product (stock mode)" or "in use by a storage location (type)". If any record uses it, the deletion is blocked and the message says who is using it. A code under approval cannot be deleted either.
The in-use check covers only the categories in the table above: categories belonging to other modules — defect reasons, downtime types, order types and so on — are not checked , so they can be deleted — and the code left on existing records can then no longer be resolved to a name. Check for yourself that nothing uses such a code before deleting it, or make it inactive instead.
The right way to retire a code that has been used is to untick "Active" rather than delete it : existing records still display correctly, and it can no longer be chosen on new ones.
The results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the category, code, Chinese and English names, sort order and active status.

Company-wide settings — users, roles, permissions, organization and plants — maintained centrally by the system administrator
The system administration screens decide who may use the system and how far they may go . The order to set things up in is: plants, organization structure, roles, permissions, then users ; doing it the other way round gets stuck — a role with no permissions shows the person nothing, however it is assigned.
Some screens are for Admin only: users, roles, organization, plants, permission settings, mobile permissions, two-step verification reset and license status appear in the menu and open only while your current role is Admin (the permission matrix does not decide them). Code maintenance, the audit log and system parameters follow the permission matrix.
Sign-in accounts, e-mail, language, and which roles each person holds.
The carrier of permissions: the role name, its organization unit, the plants allowed and the default plant.
The department tree, its levels and plant inheritance; supervisor approval walks up it to find the approver.
Plant codes, default language and time zone, and per-plant overrides of the system parameters.
The permission matrix, role by role: read, create, update, delete and print.
Action-by-action permissions for shop-floor work in the mobile app, independent of the desktop matrix.
Who changed which record and when, and what the values were before and after.
Resetting two-factor authentication for a user who has lost their authenticator.
Whether the license is valid; applying for, renewing and importing a license, and the 90-day confirmation (address /License ).
Where the options in master-data drop-downs come from: payment type, stock mode, location type and more.
Simplified inventory and manufacturing modes, the default costing method, the local currency and the supplier scorecard weights.
Read-only: see at a glance which plants override which system parameters and which follow the global value.
Each person's own screen: switch the current plant and role, and set a personal time zone.

Ask the user manual in your own words, then verify the answer against the passages it was based on.
The approval settings — templates and document types — are covered separately under Approval Management (APR) .

Menu: System Administration → License Status (address /License ) | Permission: the menu entry and every action require the current role to be Admin; anyone may view the status itself
The license status page shows whether this system's license is currently valid, and is where you apply for, renew, import and periodically confirm the license . Checking the license after installation, moving to a new computer or motherboard, and the 90-day confirmation on a virtual machine all happen on this page.
If you cannot find the way in: type /License after the site address (for example https://localhost:7054/License ). When something is wrong with the license, the notice bar at the top of every screen links here too; if the license does not belong to this computer, this is the only page the system shows.

C.H: License Status › What the page shows
C.T:
Section | Guide
Status (coloured box) | Green "License valid", with a line on binding and term (for example "Bound to this machine; No expiry date"); amber "The license needs attention" lists what to do (expiring soon, not yet confirmed); red "Read-only" or "Disabled" gives the reason and the date the system stops.
Expiry / read-only since / disabled on | A perpetual license shows "Perpetual" as its expiry. Read-only since and disabled on appear only once the license has lapsed.
License ID, licensee, binding, seats | Visible to Admin only. You need the license ID when renewing or contacting the license provider.
Apply for or renew a license | Shows the deployment type, the host check result and the request code. "Apply for a license" opens the registration page; "Request renewal" is for a new computer or motherboard. Only the fingerprint and host identifier (both hashed) are sent.
License confirmation (every 90 days) | Needed only on a virtual machine, or once online license check is turned on. "Confirm license" opens the license server's confirmation page and comes back here when done; if this computer cannot reach the internet, send the link to another device and then use "Import confirmation reply".
Online license check | A machine-bound license may turn this on: it then needs confirming every 90 days, and a copy of the whole machine elsewhere cannot pass. On a virtual machine it is always on and cannot be turned off.
Import license file | Upload the license.json you received. It is verified first and replaces the current license only if it passes (the old file is backed up); no restart is needed.
Do not edit the license file: every field is covered by the signature, so any change makes it "signature invalid". If the host check says the license does not belong to this computer, apply again with the request code on the page.
User Management (assigning the Admin role), Personal Settings (switching your current role).

Menu: System Administration → Mobile Permission Settings | Permission: current role is Admin
Mobile module permissions decide what each role may do in the mobile app (PWA) for shop-floor work. It is a separate set of permissions from the desktop "Permission Settings": ticking the desktop matrix leaves the phone closed, and the other way round.
Mobile module permission screenshot (illustrative; the modules and actions shown vary by version and by which are enabled)
The panel that opens after clicking "Set mobile permissions": grouped by module, ticked action by action, with "Select All / Deselect All" at the top right of each group

C.H: Mobile Module Permissions › Modules and actions you can grant
C.T:
Permissions are granted action by action : a person with that role can only do on the phone what has been ticked here.
Module | Actions
Production reporting | Setup before starting, start work, stop work, report production, change machine status, inspection (FPI / IPQC), viewing the production schedule (including the schedule query and the preparation board), requisition / return requests, and over-quantity approval
Warehouse operations | Put away, pick, stock enquiry, incoming inspection (IQC / FQC / RQC), stock counting, work-order issue / return, staging, outsource receiving, and over-quantity approval
Over-quantity approval is the "supervisor" right. When a plant sets "beyond the tolerance" to supervisor confirmation, only roles with this box ticked can report over-production (Production reporting) or receive outsource deliveries over the order quantity (Warehouse operations); desktop reporting and outsource receipt confirmation check the same box . New actions added by an upgrade are normally granted automatically to roles that already have the module, but these two are deliberately not — tick them for supervisors only.
The screen lists only the modules that are enabled . The system also has two further mobile modules — quality inspection and material picking — which are disabled by default and therefore do not appear here. Not seeing them is expected and is not a permission problem.

1
Choose "System Administration > Mobile Permission Settings" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to list the roles.
2
Click edit on the role; the list of modules and actions slides out on the right.
3
Tick the actions the role may perform on the phone and click "Save".
4
Shop-floor staff see the new functions after refreshing or signing in again on the phone.
Saving replaces the whole set: when you save, the system clears this role's mobile permissions entirely and writes every action back from what is ticked on screen, recording the unticked ones as not allowed. Make all your changes in one visit.
Every change here leaves an audit record: the system writes an entry to the audit log with the entity type Mobile.Permission , recording the role and how many actions were allowed. To trace when and by whom the mobile permissions were changed, go to Audit Log and filter by that entity type.

C.H: Mobile Module Permissions › Cannot sign in on the phone, or no functions appear
C.T:
Symptom | What to check first
Signs in, but the home screen has no operations | The role currently in effect for that user has no action ticked here. Note that a person may hold several roles, and what counts is the one currently in effect .
The module is visible but the action is refused | The individual action inside the module is not ticked; modules and actions are granted separately.

The list can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the role name, its Chinese name and its organization unit. As on the desktop permission screen, the export is the list of roles, not the ticks.

Menu: System Administration → Organization Structure | Permission: current role is Admin
Organization structure maintains the company's department tree . It does two things in practice: roles are attached to organization units, and supervisor approval walks up this tree to find the person above . Whether the tree is drawn correctly therefore decides directly whether approval flows can run at all.
Organization structure screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Required | Guide
Organization name | Required | The department name, for example "Production" or "Purchasing".
Parent organization |  | Left empty it becomes a top-level node (usually the company or the plant). While editing, the drop-down automatically leaves out the unit itself and everything beneath it, so the tree cannot be looped back on itself.
Plant |  | The plant this unit belongs to. It may be left empty : left empty, the plant of the parent unit applies, walking up until one is found that has a value. The list shows the result after that inheritance.
Sort order |  | The display order within one level: smaller numbers come first, and units with the same number are ordered by name.
Current path |  | Read-only and composed by the system : the parent's path, a slash, then this unit's name. Rename it or move it, and the path is recalculated on save.

Situation | What the screen shows
The search box is empty | Tree mode : the whole tree is drawn from the top-level nodes down, showing each unit's plant after inheritance.
A keyword is entered | Search mode : the units whose name or path matches are listed flat, without the tree levels.
How to read the markers on the tree
Marker | What it means
A light blue plant badge beside the name | The unit has a plant of its own .
A grey plant badge beside the name | The plant is inherited from the parent ; the unit itself has none (hovering shows a hint).
No plant badge | Neither the unit nor any unit above it has a plant.
The number in brackets after the name | How many direct child units it has — the next level only, not deeper ones.
Searching by path is useful: type the name of a higher department and every unit beneath it is listed at once, at any depth, because they all carry that name in their path.

Creating a department
1
Choose "System Administration > Organization Structure" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to load the whole tree.
2
Click "Add", enter the name and choose the parent (leave it empty for a top-level unit).
3
Choose a plant only when the unit is fixed to one; child departments within the same plant are usually left empty to inherit it.
4
Enter the sort order and click "Save"; the path is generated automatically.
Moving a department
1
Open the unit, change "Parent organization" to the new parent and save.
2
This unit's path is recalculated at once. The paths of the units beneath it, however, are not updated automatically : after moving a department that has children, open each child and save it once so that its path is regenerated.
Moving a unit changes who signs as supervisor: the supervisor is taken from the people under the parent unit , so a new parent means a new approver. Requests already submitted and still running are unaffected — their approver was decided at the moment of submission — but everything submitted afterwards follows the new route.

C.H: Organization Structure › Deleting an organization unit
C.T:
Reason it is blocked | What to do
It still has child units | Move the children to another parent or delete them too, working from the bottom up.
Roles are attached to it | Reattach those roles to another organization unit under "Role Management".
Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON can be exported, containing the name, path and sort order. The export covers every organization unit , regardless of what is in the search box on screen.

Menu: System Administration → Permission Settings | Permission: current role is Admin
Permission settings are where you decide who sees what and who may do what . Permissions are granted by role : pick a role from the list, then tick the five actions — read, create, update, delete and print — screen by screen in the permission matrix.
Not ticked means not allowed: the system works on default-deny . A screen with no "read" tick does not appear in that role's menu, and typing its address directly is blocked as well — it is not merely hidden.
Permission settings screenshot (illustrative; the modules and screens shown vary by version)
The permission matrix that opens after clicking "Set permissions": grouped by module, one screen per row and one action per column

C.H: Permission Settings › The five actions in the matrix
C.T:
Action | What it means
View (R) | The menu item is visible, the screen can be opened and the data can be queried. It is the precondition for the other four .
Create (C) | The "Add" button appears and new records can be created.
Update (U) | Existing records can be edited. On document screens, actions that change status such as posting or approving fall under this too.
Delete (D) | Records can be deleted; most screens additionally check whether the record is in use, so having the permission does not always mean it can be removed.
Print (P) | Printing and exporting (Excel, CSV, JSON) are allowed.
Some screens do not have all five actions by nature: a report has only read and print, and an audit log can hardly have create. An empty cell with no switch means the screen does not support that action , not that it was left out.

Setting the permissions of a role
1
Choose "System Administration > Permission Settings" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to list the roles.
2
Click edit on the role; the matrix slides out on the right, listing every screen grouped by module (master data, manufacturing, purchasing and so on).
3
Tick what is needed. Each module heading has a "Select all" that fills in the whole module at once.
4
Click "Save". The change takes effect immediately ; users with that role see the new menu as soon as they refresh the page.
Saving replaces the whole matrix, not just what changed: when you save, the system first clears all of this role's existing permissions and then rebuilds them from what is ticked on screen. So make all your changes in one visit , and do not save while the matrix is still loading.
The order for opening up a new role
1
Create the role under "Role Management" first, with its organization unit and allowed plants.
2
Come back here and tick the permissions.
3
Assign the role to people under "User Management".
4
If the role also uses the mobile app, set its mobile functions under "Mobile Module Permissions" as well. The two sets of permissions are independent of each other : ticking the desktop matrix does not enable anything on the phone.
Why some screens are not in the matrix: the home page and personal settings are available to everyone and are not listed. The user, role, organization, plant, permission settings, mobile permission settings, two-step verification reset and license status screens under system administration are available only while your current role is Admin , and are not listed either: those screens change who may do what, so handing them to the matrix would let anyone who can open permission settings promote themselves. Someone who belongs to Admin but has switched to another role loses these menu items and cannot open them either. Code maintenance, the audit log, system parameters, approval templates and document approval settings follow the matrix like every other screen.
The list can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the role name, its English name and its organization unit. The export is the list of roles, not the ticks in the matrix .

Menu: System Administration → Plant Management | Permission: current role is Admin
Plant management maintains the plants in the system, along with each plant's default language, time zone and parameter overrides . The plant is how data is partitioned system-wide: users see the documents and stock of the plant they are currently in, and no other.
Plant management screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Required | Guide
Plant code | Required | The unique code (for example P01); it cannot be changed once created , and every document records it as the plant it belongs to.
Plant name | Required | The Chinese name, shown in the plant switcher at the top right and on reports.
Name (EN) |  | The name shown when the interface is in English.
Address (ZH / EN) |  | The address printed on documents, one for each language.
Default language |  | The interface language used when a user with no personal language (set to "Follow plant default" in user maintenance) signs in or switches to this plant; a personal language, when set, takes priority.
Default time zone |  | Times on screen are converted using it. Internally everything is stored in UTC, so changing the time zone only affects the display and never alters the stored data. The dropdown lists every time zone the system knows and can be searched by keyword — "Taipei", for example — and the value is validated on save, so one the system does not recognize cannot be stored. This level takes precedence over each person's own time zone : once it is set, the time zone people of this plant chose under Personal Settings has no effect (see Personal Settings ).

When editing a plant the form has two tabs: "Basic information" and "Plant parameter settings". The second lets you override the global system parameters for this one plant , in two sections — inventory and manufacturing — covering simplified inventory mode, simplified manufacturing mode, the material-ready gate at start, the machine status gate at start, the lot policy, the work-order approval amount threshold, the mandatory work-order approval conditions (outsourced orders / rework orders / orders planned to finish after the order due date — when on, matching orders are always submitted regardless of the amount threshold; a work order approval flow must exist for them to be sent), the finished-goods warehouse and location, automatic rescheduling (after changes / before dispatch / daily time, sequencing rule, freeze window), and so on.
Editing a plant, on the "Plant parameter settings" tab: each parameter has an "Override" checkbox on the left, with the current global value in grey underneath
What you see | What it means
The "Override" checkbox | Ticked means this plant sets the parameter itself; unticked means the global system parameter applies.
The "Global value" note under the field | The current global value. When the parameter is overridden it is struck through, showing that this plant does not use it.
The yellow badge beside a section heading | How many parameters in that section are overridden; "All inherited" means the section follows the global settings entirely.
Changing a value without ticking "Override" has no effect: while "Override" is unticked the control on the right can still be clicked and changed, but on save the system ignores it and clears any existing override for this plant . The checkbox is always what counts, not what you did to the value control. To drop an override and go back to the global value, untick the box and save.
Machine status gate at start: checked when work is started (desktop and mobile). If the machine is not in a schedulable state (breakdown, maintenance, external repair and so on; "standby" follows the "Standby Machines Schedulable" parameter) — None starts as usual; Warning (the default when not set) starts but reminds the user to check the machine status; Block does not allow the start. We suggest running with "Warning" for a while, until the shop floor reliably updates the status once a machine is repaired, before switching to "Block" — otherwise a repaired machine whose status was never updated cannot be started.
Over-production and outsource over-receipt: "In-plant over-production tolerance" lets the cumulative good quantity reported exceed the dispatch quantity by that percentage (at 3%, a dispatch of 100 can be reported up to 103); not set = 0, not a single unit more. Beyond that, "In-plant: beyond the tolerance" either rejects it (the default) or requires supervisor confirmation — only roles granted "Over-quantity approval" under Mobile Module Permissions can report it (the same right applies on desktop and mobile). Outsource receipts have the same pair, "Outsource over-receipt tolerance" and "Outsource: beyond the tolerance" (default: supervisor confirmation), plus "Processing fee for the over-received quantity": Pay (default) or Do not pay — with "Do not pay" the AP invoice covers only the ordered quantity, and the receipt line remarks record the contract price and the billed quantity.
Simplified outsourcing (all off by default): When "Deduct outsource send-out materials automatically at receipt" is on, no separate outsource material issue is needed: each time an outsource receipt is confirmed, the system works out the quantity due as work-order material × cumulative quantity received ÷ work-order quantity , subtracts what has already been issued (net of returns), and creates and posts an outsource issue slip for the difference (taken from the product category's default location; if there is none, it stops and says so). A fully outsourced order deducts all its materials, an outsourced operation only that operation's; anything issued manually earlier is not deducted again. When "Inspect outsource deliveries at receipt" is on, each line of mobile Outsource Receiving gets a Defects field: submitting completes the inspection (MIL-STD-1916, Ac=0). 0 defects = pass, stocked straight into a normal warehouse (the line location, or the product category default) and added to the outsourced dispatch's completed quantity; any defect = the whole lot goes to the plant's quarantine warehouse for nonconformance handling and does not count as completed. Inspection-exempt products go straight to a normal warehouse. No "Putaway → Incoming Inspection" steps are needed, even in non-simplified plants; desktop receipts keep the normal flow. When "Create the outsource PO automatically when an outsourced work order is released" is on, releasing an outsourced work order creates a Confirmed outsource PO for the single supplier with a valid quotation (see the Outsource PO page for details).

Adding a plant
1
Choose "System Administration > Plant Management" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to load the existing plants.
2
Click "Add", enter the plant code and name, set the default language and time zone, and save.
3
Once the plant exists, tick it into the relevant roles' allowed plants under "Role Management"; until then nobody can enter it.
4
A new plant usually needs its own warehouses, storage locations, document number settings and accounting periods, created on the respective master-data screens.
Turning on simplified mode for one plant
1
Open the plant and switch to the "Plant parameter settings" tab.
2
Find simplified manufacturing mode, tick "Override" first , then switch the toggle on the right to on.
3
Reopen it after saving and the yellow "N overridden" badge appears beside the section heading, showing that the override is in place.

Reason it is blocked | What to do
Users are currently in this plant | Ask them to switch to another plant first.
Organization units point to it | Change or clear the plant on those units under "Organization Structure".
Roles list it as an allowed plant | Untick it under "Role Management".
A plant that has been in use cannot in practice be deleted, and should not be: documents, stock and journal entries all reference it. To retire one, remove it from every role's allowed plants and nobody can switch into it again.

Route: /QaAssistant | Ask the user manual in your own words, then verify the answer against its sources
This screen lets you ask in your own words — for example "which screen shows materials with no movement for a long time" — without having to know what the function is called. The system first finds the most relevant passages in the user manual, hands them to the local language model together with your question, and then shows the answer alongside the passages it was based on.
Ask the Manual screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)
There are two modes at the top of the screen, and you choose which one — the system never guesses for you : "Manual Q&A" reads the user manual and the rule notes, while "Data query" reads your own operational data. They differ in source, permissions and how much you should trust them, which is why they are kept apart.

It answers "where to look, how to do it, what the rule says" — not "what your numbers are". It reads the user manual, not your database: in this mode, asking "what was last month's purchase amount" will not return a figure, only which report shows it.

C.H: Ask the Manual › How to use it
C.T:
1
Type your question in the box at the bottom and click Send. Keep it under 500 characters.
2
Wait for the answer. Inference runs on the local CPU and a question takes about a minute ; the input box is locked meanwhile and shows how long you have waited. Click Cancel if you do not want to wait — this genuinely stops the computation, not just the display.
3
Open the "Sources" below the answer and check that the passage really supports it. This step is not optional: the model blends two passages into one fluent paragraph, and fluent is not the same as correct.

C.H: Ask the Manual › The three kinds of source
C.T:
Appearance | What it means
A clickable link | A page of this user manual; click it for the full instructions for that screen.
An expandable passage (its page code starts with rules/ ) | A rule explanation. This kind of content has no manual page of its own, so the full text is expanded right below the answer instead. These passages currently exist in Chinese only , so when you ask in English the answer comes back in English while this kind of citation stays in Chinese. That is deliberate: matching the language here would leave an English question with no rule passages at all, and on screen that looks exactly like "the manual never covered it".
Grey plain text marked "cannot be verified" | The model cited a page that was not supplied to it this time — in other words, it made the reference up. That part of the answer has no basis; do not rely on it, and confirm another way.

Switch to "Data query" and you can query operational data in one sentence — for example "which items have available stock below their safety level". The system picks one of the existing report queries, fills in its conditions, runs it, and returns a table with a plain-language summary. The query is run by the system, not by the model : the model only decides which query to use and what conditions to fill in, plus writes the closing summary. It never touches the database.
1
If a confirmation block appears first, read the conditions before pressing "Confirm and run". Two situations trigger it: the query returns monetary amounts (several costing bases run in parallel here, and the wrong one still yields plausible figures), or your question may match more than one query , in which case a selector appears above. You can edit any condition; clearing a field means "not specified". "Discard this query" runs nothing. Nothing has been queried yet at that point.
2
Open "Query parameters" above the table and check that the conditions really match what you asked. This is no more optional than checking sources in Manual Q&A: the model sometimes fills in conditions you never mentioned — most often the period — and the value it picks looks entirely reasonable and the figures are self-consistent. You cannot tell without checking.
3
A question takes two inference passes (choosing the query, then writing the summary), so it is slower than Manual Q&A. If the summary times out the table is still shown, with a note saying the summary was skipped — the data had already been retrieved by then.
4
When there are many rows only the first 200 are shown, together with the total count; open the corresponding report screen for the complete set.
5
Once you have the result you wanted, name it below and save it as a favourite query. What is saved is the conditions , not the results: opening it later runs the query again and re-checks your permissions. ⚠️ If the confirmation message says some conditions "were not saved", the report screen has no matching field for them — that saved query is broader than the question you asked and its figures will be larger. To receive it regularly, add a schedule for it on the report schedule screen.
If nothing fits, it says there is no matching query rather than substituting other data. Only some reports are reachable this way — reports containing monetary amounts (sales value, inventory value, cost) are not available through natural language by default and must be opened from their report screens, even if you have permission for them. This is deliberate: repeatedly probing the same data one sentence at a time is not the same risk as opening a report step by step. Your system administrator decides whether to open it up.
You can only reach reports you are already allowed to open. Plant and data-scope restrictions apply exactly as before — asking and clicking give you the same slice of data.

C.H: Ask the Manual › Points to note
C.T:
If the manual does not cover it, the answer is simply "not found in the user manual". That is correct behaviour, not a fault: saying so is more useful to you than inventing a plausible-looking set of steps.
It can only find screens you are allowed to see. Retrieval is filtered by the role you are currently using, so the same question may be answered differently for different roles, and screens you have no permission for never appear as sources.
One question at a time per person. Sending another while the previous one is still running is refused with a prompt to wait or cancel — this is not a fault. Inference runs on a single local CPU, and running two questions at once merely makes both slower. If the whole machine is busy you will see "inference service is busy"; wait and retry, or simply open the report screen instead — that path does not involve inference and is always immediate.
Your questions are not kept. Neither the question nor the answer is written to any index or table; they are gone when you leave the page and can never turn up in anyone else's results. By the same token the assistant does not remember your previous question — each one stands alone.
A yellow "inference service is not ready" banner means the local language model is not running or the model files are not installed; the message says which. You can still open the screen but cannot get answers — contact your system administrator.

C.H: Ask the Manual › Rebuilding the index
C.T: The Rebuild index button in the top right is only visible to roles with update permission on this screen. After the manual is updated the index refreshes automatically at the next system start; this button is for when you want it to take effect without a restart. Rebuilding uses inference resources, but questions always take priority — the rebuild yields whenever someone is asking, so it will not hold anyone up; the cost is that the rebuild itself takes longer when the system is busy (possibly well over several minutes). Avoiding busy periods is still advisable.
System Parameters

Menu: System Administration → Role Management | Permission: current role is Admin
A role is the one and only carrier of permissions in this system: which menus a user sees, and whether they may create or delete, is decided entirely by the roles assigned to them. Roles themselves are created and maintained on this screen, while what each role may actually do is set on the Permission Settings screen.
Role management screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Required | Guide
Role name | Required | Unique across the system. It is the name shown on approval template steps that target a role, and in the permission settings list.
Name (EN) |  | The name shown when the interface is in English. Left empty, the Chinese name is shown in the English interface too.
Organization unit |  | The department this role belongs to. It is not merely descriptive: supervisor approval uses it to find the person above (see below).
Plants allowed |  | Tick the plants this role may enter. Ticking none means no restriction , and the user may switch to any plant in the system.
Default plant |  | The plant a user lands in when they switch to this role. When plants are ticked but no default is chosen, the first one in the list is used.

C.H: Role Management › Organization unit and supervisor approval
C.T:
A step in an approval template can name the approver as "supervisor". This is how the system works out who that is:
1
Take the role that was in effect for the requester when they submitted .
2
Find the organization unit that role is attached to, then go up to its parent organization unit .
3
Among the roles attached to that parent unit, take one of their users as the approver.
A role with no organization unit makes supervisor approval stall silently: if any of the three steps above comes up empty — the role has no organization unit, the unit has no parent, or no user sits under the parent unit — no approver can be resolved. The document is then still submitted, yet appears in nobody's "My Pending Approvals" , and there is no error message. To find such documents, go to "All Approval Requests" and tick Unassigned only , then fill in the approver with "Reassign".

When a user switches role under "Personal settings" after signing in, the system handles the plant at the same time:
The role's plant setting | When switching to this role
Plants are ticked | The user is moved to the default plant (or the first one if no default is set), and may only switch among the ticked plants .
No plant is ticked | The user stays in the plant they are in and may switch to any plant.

Adding a role
1
Choose "System Administration > Role Management" in the left-hand menu and click "Search" to load the existing roles.
2
Click "Add", fill in the role name and its English name, and choose the organization unit it belongs to.
3
Tick the plants allowed and mark one of them as the default.
4
Click "Save". At this point the role has no permissions at all ; you must go on to "Permission Settings" and tick the screens and actions.
5
Finally, assign the role to the people who will use it under "User Management".

Any of the following blocks the deletion, and the message lists the reason:
Reason it is blocked | What to do
Users still have it (the count is shown) | Untick this role for those people under "User Management" first.
An approval template step targets it | Change that step to another role, or delete it, under "Approval Template Settings".
An approval flow submitted under this role is still running | Wait for it to finish or be withdrawn.
Deleting also clears the permission settings: once the checks pass, the system also deletes this role's permission matrix , and clears it for users who currently have it in effect. If you recreate a role with the same name afterwards, its permissions have to be ticked again.
The results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the role name, its English name and its organization unit.

Menu: System Administration → System Parameters | Permissions: read / change
System parameters are shared company-wide settings for the whole company, not per plant. Once changed, takes effect immediately (no restart needed), but because it reaches every module, it should be maintained centrally by the system administrator.
Note: The parameter only affects after it is changed newly created documents does not go back and rewrite existing documents . Turning on simplified manufacturing mode, for example, does not turn work orders that were already exploded and are still "planned" into "released".
System parameter screenshot (illustrative; the actual sections and options vary by version and permission)

Parameter | Default | Guide
Simplified inventory mode | Close | controls When posting happens . With it on, an inventory document posts as soon as it is created or approved, instead of going through the two stages of creating and then posting. It suits small warehouses that do not need documents to be reviewed.
Default costing method | Moving average (MA) | The inventory costing method for the whole system: moving average or first-in first-out (FIFO).

Parameter | Default | Guide
Simplified Manufacturing Mode | Close | controls Process gates . With it on, work orders go straight to "released" as soon as the MRP run finishes, with no need to go to the work order or production batch screen and click "Release".
Reschedule automatically after changes | Off | After a release, split, machine switch, completion, cancellation, machine status change, work calendar change or planned downtime change, the schedule is re-run once things have been quiet for 90 seconds (at most 10 minutes while changes keep coming).
Reschedule automatically before dispatch | Off | If the schedule is out of date, it is re-run (a few seconds) before Dispatch Operations, the mobile dispatch list, the Preparation Board or Production Schedule opens, and before the 17:00 preparation alert is sent.
Daily automatic rescheduling time (HH:mm) | Not used | A full re-run once a day at this time; set it before the 17:00 preparation alert, for example 16:00. If the time is missed (for example the server was off) it runs later the same day, and never twice on one day.
Sequencing rule for automatic runs | Not set (Priority) | Automatic runs sequence production batches by this rule (Priority, Earliest Due Date, Shortest Process Time, FIFO, LIFO). It is also the default rule on the Production Schedule screen; a manual run can still pick another.
Freeze window (hours) | Not used | In automatic runs, scheduled dispatches starting within this many hours keep their machine and time slot — 24, for example, means nothing due to start before this time tomorrow is moved by an automatic run. Blank or 0 turns it off; at most 168. Manual runs ignore it.
The three kinds of automatic rescheduling can be combined, and each plant can override all five settings above on the parameter tab of Plant Management . How it works is described under Production Schedule → Automatic rescheduling .
What changes when simplified manufacturing mode is on
Step | Off (default) | On
MRP Run | Create it by hand, pick the order lines to explode and click "Run MRP" | Created and run automatically once the order is approved ; the message shown after saving tells you the run number that was created
MRP run | creates the production batch and the work orders, with a work order status of Planned | the same, except that the run is followed by an automatic release
Release | Someone goes to the work order or production batch screen and clicks "Release"; the system recalculates the demand and checks for shortages, and a shortage blocks the release | this step disappears ; the quantity is the planned quantity from the run, and a shortage does not block the document
Approval | may need to be submitted for approval, depending on the approval settings | treated as approved , without approval. Exception: if the plant has a work order approval flow and has explicitly set an amount threshold (for orders above it) or turned on a mandatory approval condition (outsourced / rework / delayed), matching work orders are still submitted and can be started only after approval
Material Requisitions | Created automatically when the release is approved (push material) | the same, generated automatically
Outsource purchase order | Created automatically when an outsource work order is released | the same, created automatically
Scheduling | It has to be scheduled first: the dispatch has to move from "to be scheduled" to "scheduled" before work can start | this step can be skipped ; work can start even while the dispatch is still "to be scheduled", and such dispatches appear in the shop-floor to-do list
Start / finish / report | works as usual | the way it works is the same ; plus an operation sequence check (see below)
Operation sequence check (simplified mode only): without a schedule there is nothing to guarantee that earlier operations are done first, so when production is reported the system checks that this operation's cumulative completed quantity cannot exceed the previous operation of the previous operation, and rejects the report if it goes over (so you never get the impossible figure of a later process producing more than an earlier one). The first operation is exempt. With simplified mode off, Not done this check, keeping the existing approach of letting the schedule guarantee the order.
Shortages no longer block the document: With it on, a work order short of material is still released; its material status simply shows "short", and the MRP result screen lists a message. The check on shortages moves to Start work , the material check at that point (the "material ready gate at start" parameter decides whether it warns or blocks). Make sure the shop floor can live with the change before turning it on.
An automatic run only covers the quantity not yet exploded: The system works on order quantity minus the quantity already exploded, so saving the same order again does not exploding it twice. If the order later Increase , the next approval only explodes the additional quantity. An order Update (changing the quantity or the delivery date) works as before — it simply marks the related MRP run as needing a re-run, is not re-run automatically , because a re-run would affect released work orders and received purchase orders, so someone has to decide.
Also note: if your orders have Approval flow and the approval is given on the "Pending my approval" screen, that order waits for the next order approval before it is exploded; with simplified mode the recommendation is not to put an approval flow on orders at all.
The two "simplified modes" are not the same: Simplified inventory mode governs When posting happens (whether posting takes two stages), while simplified manufacturing mode governs Process gates (whether release has to be done by hand). The two are independent and either can be turned on alone; turning on simplified inventory mode does not also turn on simplified manufacturing mode.

Parameter | Default | Guide
Local Amount | Not set | The currency the company's books are kept in, the basis of every conversion. The dropdown only lists Active currencies; create it under "Currency Maintenance" first and then come back to set it.

Weight of this item in the supplier's total score; the four weights do not have to add up to exactly 100, as the system scales them proportionally. Leave it blank to go back to the default.
Parameter | Default | Guide
Quality weight | 30 | Weight given to quality aspects such as the incoming inspection pass rate
Delivery weight | 30 | Weight given to the on-time delivery rate
Price weight | 20 | Weight given to how competitive the quotes are
Service weight | 20 | Weight given to cooperativeness, responsiveness and the like
Input limits: The weight only accepts 0 or a positive number . If a negative or non-numeric value is entered, the field is not saved , and keeps its original value — after saving, check that the figure on the screen is the one you meant.

Menu: System Administration → Two-Factor Reset | Permission: current role is Admin
Two-factor administration is the rescue screen for a lost authenticator : when somebody changes phone, deletes their authenticator app and has run out of or lost their recovery codes, an administrator resets their two-factor authentication here.
Two-factor administration screenshot (illustrative; the data shown depends on the search)

Field | Guide
User name / e-mail | How the user is identified. The search box above matches on both.
Two-factor status | Enabled or not. Only an enabled one has anything to reset.
Reset | Turns two-factor authentication off for that user and clears their authenticator key. Somebody whose status is "not enabled" has no such button — the column shows a dash, because there is nothing to reset.
Unlike the other search screens, this one lists users as soon as you open it , with no need to click "Search" first. At most 200 rows are shown, so use the search box to narrow it down when there are many people.

Resetting two-factor authentication for a user
1
Confirm who is asking by some other means first — in person, by telephone or through their manager. This action removes the second line of defence on that account.
2
Choose "System Administration > Two-Factor Reset" in the left-hand menu and type the user name or e-mail in the search box.
3
Find the user and click "Reset"; a confirmation message appears at the top of the screen.
4
Ask them to sign in again; the system will require them to re-enrol an authenticator and take a fresh set of recovery codes.
A reset invalidates the old key and all old recovery codes: after the reset the codes produced by the authenticator already on their phone no longer work , and any recovery codes printed earlier are void as well. If they have in fact only moved the authenticator to a new phone and still have the key, do not reset .

C.H: Two-Factor Reset › Who must have two-factor authentication
C.T:
By default the system requires it for the Admin role : somebody with the administrator role who has not yet enabled it is taken straight to the setup screen after signing in and cannot use anything else until enrolment is complete.
Situation | Result
A role that is required to have it, not yet enabled | Redirected to the two-factor setup page after sign-in; nothing else until enrolment is done.
Other roles | Not required, but they may enable it themselves on their own two-factor setup page.
After a reset | If they belong to a role that requires it, they are asked to enrol again at their next sign-in. That is expected, not a failed reset.
Which roles are required to use it, and whether the requirement is switched off altogether, are deployment-level settings rather than something changed on screen; ask whoever maintains the installation. Roles used on shared shop-floor terminals are usually left out of the requirement on purpose.

Menu: Personal Settings | Permission: available to everyone who can sign in
Personal settings is the one screen that belongs to each person : switch the current plant, switch the current role, set a personal time zone and look at your own account details. Nothing here affects anybody else, and no administrator permission is needed.
Personal settings screenshot (illustrative; the plants and roles you can switch to depend on what you have been assigned)

C.H: Personal Settings › Sections of the screen
C.T:
Section | Guide
Switch Active Plant | Lists every plant you are assigned to, with the one you are in now marked "In Use". After switching, every document and stock figure in the system is that of the new plant only . If the role currently in effect restricts which plants are available, a notice says so at the top.
Switch Active Role | A person may hold several roles, but only one is in effect at a time . The one in effect decides which menus you see and who approves the documents you submit. The organization unit is shown under each role name; a role with no organization unit is shown as a system role.
Personal Time Zone | The time zone in effect is shown first, with a small label saying which level it came from — from plant setting, from personal setting, or system default. The dropdown below sets your own, and leaving it empty means follow the plant time zone .
Account Information | Read-only: user name, e-mail and current plant. To change the account name or e-mail, ask an administrator to do it on the user management screen.

C.H: Personal Settings › How the time zone is decided
C.T:
Every time shown on screen is converted using a three-level order of precedence . Internally everything is stored in universal time; the conversion affects only what is displayed and how date filters are interpreted, never the stored data.
Order | Source
First | The default time zone of the plant you are in, set on the plant management screen.
Second | Your personal time zone, set here — an administrator can also set it for you on the user management screen.
Last | The system default, Asia/Taipei.
When the plant has a time zone of its own, your personal time zone does not take effect — and that is not a failed save. The screen says outright which plant time zone is overriding it; the value you saved is kept, and is used as soon as you switch to a plant that has none.

Switching to another plant
1
Choose "Personal Settings" in the left-hand menu.
2
Find the plant you want under Switch Active Plant and click "Switch to This Plant".
3
Search again on whatever list you were looking at; the results already on screen are still those of the previous plant.
Switching the role in effect
1
Find the role you want under Switch Active Role and click "Switch to This".
2
The left-hand menu is rebuilt for the permissions of the new role, so screens you could see before may disappear. That is expected.
Setting a personal time zone
1
Type a keyword into the dropdown under Personal Time Zone to find a zone — Taipei or Shanghai, for example — or pick "Follow plant time zone" to clear the setting.
2
Click "Save time zone". A confirmation appears when it is stored; if the zone cannot be resolved by the system an error is shown and nothing is saved.
3
Look back at the time zone in effect and check whether the label now reads "from personal setting"; if it still says "from plant setting", the plant time zone is overriding yours.
The plant at the top shows a yellow "Plant no longer available — please choose again": an administrator removed your current plant from your role, so every screen sends you here first. Pick an available plant under Switch Active Plant and everything works again.
Plant and role are two different things: the plant decides whose data you see , the role decides what you may do and who approves your documents . Check both before submitting anything for approval: the same document submitted under a different role goes down a different approval flow.
User Management (an administrator sets the language and personal time zone on somebody's behalf), Plant Management (the plant default time zone), Role Management (which plants a role may use).

Menu: System Administration → User Management | Permission: current role is Admin
User management maintains the sign-in accounts of the system: the user name, the e-mail address, the interface language, and which roles the person has been given. A user carries no permissions of their own: permissions always sit on the role , so assigning a role is what actually grants access.
System administrators only: This screen — and role, organization, plant, permission settings, mobile permissions and two-step verification reset with it — is available only while the current role is Admin ; someone who belongs to Admin but has switched to another role cannot open it either. These screens are not set in the permission matrix.
User management screenshot (illustrative; actual fields and data vary by permission and query criteria)

Field | Required | Guide
User name | Required | The name typed at sign-in; unique across the system. This is the name recorded in the audit log.
E-mail | Required | Also the value typed into the "E-mail" box on the sign-in page. It is marked as confirmed on creation; no verification mail is sent.
Initial password | Required | Appears only when creating a user; it is not shown when editing an existing one, and a password cannot be changed here (see "What to do about a forgotten password" below).
Language |  | Appears only when editing ; choose "Follow plant default", Traditional Chinese or English from the list. A chosen language always takes priority; "Follow plant default" (empty) uses the default language of the user's current plant when signing in or switching plants. Once the user switches language on screen, that choice is saved as their personal language.
Personal Time Zone |  | Appears only when editing . Left empty it means follow the plant time zone , which is what most accounts should be; the value takes effect only when the plant the person is currently in has no time zone of its own.
Roles |  | You may tick more than one . Each role in the list shows "organization unit / plants it may use" in brackets, for example "(Head Office / ADM, P1, P2)"; a role with no organization unit shows "System", and a role not restricted to particular plants shows "all plants". After signing in the user switches the role currently in effect under "Personal settings".

Searching for a user
1
Choose "System Administration > User Management" in the left-hand menu.
2
Type part of a user name or e-mail address in the search bar (leave it empty for everyone) and click "Search".
3
Click a column heading to sort by it (user name, e-mail or language); the page size can be changed below the list.
The list is empty when you first open the screen. That does not mean there is no data: every search screen in this system loads its data only after "Search" is clicked.
Adding a user
1
Click "Add" in the top right corner; the form slides out on the right.
2
Fill in the user name, the e-mail address and the initial password.
3
Tick the roles this person should have (more than one is allowed, and they can be added later).
4
Click "Save". If the password does not meet the rules, the message appears at the top of the form.
Changing someone's roles
1
Find the user and click edit in the list to open the form.
2
Tick the roles to add and untick the ones to remove, then click "Save". The system adds what is newly ticked and removes what is no longer ticked.
Removing a role changes what the person sees immediately: if the role removed happens to be the one currently in effect for that person, their menu and the functions available to them change with it. It is worth checking that they have no work in progress before you change it.

Rule | Guide
Length | At least 8 characters.
Composition | It must contain a digit, an upper-case letter and a lower-case letter. Whether a special character is compulsory is decided by the system configuration, and by default it is not required .
Weak-password block | A password that matches the user name or e-mail address, or that appears in the common weak-password dictionary, is rejected even when the length and composition are fine.
Account lockout | After 5 failed sign-in attempts in a row the account is locked for 30 minutes ; this applies to newly created accounts too.
What to do about a forgotten password: editing here does not cover passwords. The user can reset their own through the forgotten-password flow on the sign-in page; if they are locked out because they lost their two-factor authenticator, use the "Two-Factor Administration" screen to reset it for them instead.

The system blocks the deletion and tells you why when any of the following is true of the user:
Reason it is blocked | What to do
An approval flow they started is still running | Wait for the flow to finish, or have them (or an administrator) withdraw the request.
An approval flow is waiting for them to sign | Reassign the approver of that request to somebody else under "All Approval Requests" first, then delete.
It is better not to delete somebody who has left: deleting removes the account from the system, while the audit log and the approval history keep the user name recorded at the time. The safer approach is to remove all of their roles , so that they see no functions after signing in while the account itself is kept.
The results can be exported as Excel (.xlsx), CSV or JSON, containing the user name, e-mail, language and list of roles, with the current search criteria and sort order applied.
